research.summary:
VERDICT for CIPHER: 2:4 structured sparsity is the ONE post-hoc math lever that the founding research missed, BUT it does NOT deliver the hoped-for ~2x tokens/sec at <1% quality on a frozen model. Two separate things must be true and only ONE is achievable cheaply.

(A) QUALITY requires model co-design, not post-hoc. One-shot 2:4 pruning (SparseGPT/Wanda) on a frozen Llama-2-7B is NOT quality-preserving: WikiText PPL jumps to ~14.1 (2:4 SparseGPT) vs ~5 dense, i.e. a large, unacceptable degradation — this is the same "structure-doesn't-exist-post-hoc" wall the founding hit. Quality is recovered ONLY with light continued-pretraining/finetune: Red Hat/Neural-Magic 2:4 Sparse-Llama-2-7B reaches 98.4% recovery on Open-LLM-Leaderboard-v1 (97.3% Mosaic Gauntlet) but needed SparseGPT prune + ~13B tokens of sparse retraining (26 h on 32xH100). So the lever is "needs-finetune," squarely the CO-DESIGN regime the key question asks about — and there it WORKS (<~2% avg recovery gap, full recovery on fine-tuned downstream tasks). Pure post-hoc fails the <1% bar.

(B) SPEED: hardware 2:4 raises tokens/sec but far less than 2x, and the gain is mostly a memory-traffic effect, not the FLOP-halving. On H100, sparsity ALONE delivers only ~1.2-1.3x (Red Hat Hopper FP8 article: "30% lower latency / 20% higher throughput from sparsity"; Sparse-Llama A100 single-stream sparsity-only ~1.1x). The honest mechanism: decode is memory-bound at low/mid batch, so halving FLOPs barely moves tokens/sec — exactly the FLOP-vs-MFU trap flagged. The genuine ~1.7x latency / 1.5x throughput end-to-end on H100 appears ONLY when 2:4 is COMBINED with FP8/INT4 quantization (Sparse-Marlin / sparse-FP8 CUTLASS), because quantization is what cuts the weight bytes that bound decode; the GEMM kernels themselves hit up to 2.5x (FP8+2:4) and Sparse-Marlin adds ~+65% over dense-Marlin. Prefill (compute-bound, large M) is where 2:4 approaches its 2x: A100 INT8 prefill ~1.7x, but H100 only ~1.34-1.45x because the dense H100 baseline is already very well optimized — so the 2x peak is structurally hard to realize on H100 specifically.

CAN A SUBSTRATE HOST IT? YES, cleanly. A 2:4-pruned (optionally +FP8/INT4) checkpoint is just weights + a sparse GEMM kernel (cuSPARSELt / CUTLASS sparse-FP8 / Sparse-Marlin), already merged into vLLM (PRs #10995, W4A16+2:4). This is exactly CIPHER's "host a modified checkpoint like a quantized one" path — no model retrain by the substrate, just serve the pre-pruned-and-recovered checkpoint and intercept the GEMM. The model-side prune+finetune is done offline by whoever produces the checkpoint.

BOTTOM LINE for CIPHER: 2:4 is a REAL but modest single-GPU win (~1.2-1.3x sparsity-only; ~1.5-1.7x e2e only when stacked with quantization), it is hostable by the substrate unchanged, but it is NOT post-hoc free — it requires offline prune+~13B-token finetune to stay within ~1-2% quality. It does not break the decode memory-bound ceiling on its own; quantization remains the larger lever and 2:4 is a multiplier on top of it.

methods.name: 2:4 Sparse Llama-2-7B (SparseGPT prune + sparse continued-pretrain) — sparsity ALONE
methods.math: Semi-structured 2:4 weight sparsity (50% of weights zero, 2 nonzero per contiguous 4) executed on NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores (2x peak FLOPs). Prune via SparseGPT (layerwise Hessian-based one-shot), then freeze mask + continued sparse pretraining to recover quality. Sparse GEMM via cuSPARSELt/CUTLASS.
methods.measured_speedup: Sparsity-alone: ~1.1-1.3x on H100/A100 (Red Hat Hopper article: '30% lower latency / 20% higher throughput from sparsity'; Sparse-Llama A100 single-stream sparsity contribution ~1.1x; A5000 throughput sparsity-only 1.2-1.8x). Far below the 2x peak because decode is memory-bound and the dense H100 GEMM baseline is already highly optimized.
methods.measured_quality: 98.4% recovery on Open-LLM-Leaderboard-v1, 97.3% on Mosaic Eval Gauntlet vs dense Llama-2-7B (~1.6-2.7% avg gap). Fine-tuned downstream tasks (math/code/chat) reach FULL recovery and sometimes beat dense.
methods.posthoc_possible: NO for quality at this sparsity. One-shot SparseGPT 2:4 without finetune gives WikiText PPL ~14.1 vs ~5 dense (large degradation, fails <1% bar). Quality only recovers after ~13B-token sparse retraining (26 h on 32xH100). The PRUNE step is post-hoc/one-shot; the RECOVERY step is a light finetune.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores (Ampere A100 / Hopper H100). Runs in vLLM 0.6.4 with Sparse-Marlin / CUTLASS sparse kernels.

methods.name: 2:4 Sparse Llama-2-7B + FP8 quantization (sparse-FP8 CUTLASS v3.6) — the COMBINED lever on H100
methods.math: Stack 2:4 weight sparsity with FP8 (dynamic per-token activations, static per-channel weights). Sparse Tensor Cores process 2:4 at 2x peak; FP8 cuts weight bytes loaded per decode step (attacks the memory-bound bottleneck). Custom sparse-FP8 CUTLASS v3.6 kernels.
methods.measured_speedup: End-to-end on H100: 1.7x lower single-stream latency, 1.5x higher multi-stream throughput vs dense BF16. GEMM kernels up to 2.5x (FP8+2:4 vs BF16). Sparsity contributes ~1.2-1.3x of this; FP8 supplies the rest by cutting decode memory traffic.
methods.measured_quality: 'Near-full accuracy recovery' matching prior INT8 results on GSM8K, HumanEval, AlpacaEval (no single percentage given; comparable to the ~98% recovery of the BF16 2:4 model).
methods.posthoc_possible: PARTIAL. FP8 quantization is applied post-training (calibration only), but it sits on top of the already-finetuned 2:4 checkpoint — so the underlying sparse model still required the ~13B-token recovery finetune. FP8 layer alone is post-hoc/calibration.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA Hopper H100 (FP8 + Sparse Tensor Cores). Custom sparse-FP8 CUTLASS v3.6 kernels merged into vLLM (PR #10995).

methods.name: Sparse-Marlin (2:4 + W4A16 INT4) kernel in vLLM
methods.math: Extend the Marlin mixed-precision (4-bit weight, 16-bit activation) GEMM to the 2:4 Sparse-Tensor-Core format. 4-bit weights cut memory traffic; 2:4 adds the sparse tensor-core 2x compute path. Batch-size dependent (decode memory-bound at low batch, compute-bound at high batch).
methods.measured_speedup: Sparse-Marlin adds up to +65% over dense Marlin. Marlin alone ~3.9x vs FP16 at batch 16-32 on A10, decaying to ~1.5x at batch 128 (becomes compute-bound). Llama-2-7B on RTX A6000: Marlin ~2.8x latency reduction, Sparse-Marlin ~3.3x. (A10/A6000 numbers; H100 e2e sparse+quant ~1.5-1.7x as above.)
methods.measured_quality: W4A16 + 2:4 reported as 'minimal degradation' on top of the 2:4-recovered checkpoint; recovery comparable to the BF16 2:4 model (~98%). Quality depends on the underlying finetuned sparse checkpoint, not the kernel.
methods.posthoc_possible: PARTIAL. INT4 quant is post-hoc GPTQ-style calibration, but preserves a pre-existing 2:4 mask that itself came from prune+finetune. Kernel is drop-in; the sparse checkpoint is not free.
methods.hardware: Ampere/Hopper Sparse Tensor Cores; integrated in nm-vllm / vLLM (2:4 + W4A16 feature, issue #10260).

methods.name: One-shot post-hoc 2:4 prune (SparseGPT / Wanda) — NO finetune (the FROZEN-MODEL baseline)
methods.math: SparseGPT: layerwise Hessian-based weight selection + closed-form weight update to satisfy the 2:4 mask. Wanda: weight-times-activation-norm magnitude scoring, no weight update. Both operate on the frozen pretrained model with only a small calibration set (no gradient training).
methods.measured_speedup: Same kernel speedups as above when run on Sparse Tensor Cores (~1.2-1.3x sparsity-only on H100; ~1.7x A100 INT8 prefill; H100 INT8 prefill 1.34-1.45x). Speed is identical to the finetuned model — only QUALITY differs.
methods.measured_quality: FAILS the <1% bar. LLaMA-2-7B 2:4 SparseGPT WikiText PPL ~14.13 (vs ~5 dense); 50% unstructured SparseGPT PPL ~7.01. 2:4 last layer especially sensitive (often kept dense). Wanda slightly worse than SparseGPT at 2:4 for 7B. Confirms the founding research conclusion: structure does not exist post-hoc at 2:4 on a 7B without recovery.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES (this IS the pure post-hoc option) — but it does NOT preserve quality at 2:4 on 7B-dense. This is the negative result confirming co-design is required.
methods.hardware: Any Sparse-Tensor-Core GPU (A100/H100); checkpoint hostable in vLLM.

assessment.method: 2:4 semi-structured weight sparsity on Sparse-Llama-2-7B (SparseGPT one-shot Hessian prune → freeze mask → sparse continued-pretraining + SquareHead KD), executed on NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores via cuSPARSELt/CUTLASS, served under vLLM/compressed-tensors.
assessment.honest_gain: Honest H100 / 7B-dense / quality-preserved throughput gain from sparsity ALONE: ~1.1-1.3x, and ONLY in the favorable regime (large-batch prefill / compute-bound, M>=~2048). At decode (small M, memory-bound — CIPHER's dominant regime) the gain collapses to ~1.0x, and on realistic 7B layer shapes PyTorch's H100 2:4 GEMM is measured at 0.37-0.67x i.e. SLOWER than dense (issue #153825); it only beats dense (2.1x) at a 30720x102400 matrix no 7B layer contains. Standalone cuSPARSELt tops ~1.6x; SlideSparse measures 1.34-1.5x at large-M only. Red Hat's vendor 'up to 30% lower latency / 20% higher throughput' (~1.2-1.3x, batch-1/small-batch, favorable framing) is the realistic ceiling. The advertised 2.1-3.0x and HPC-AI's 1.27x e2e are sparsity+quant (W4A16/FP8) combined, NOT sparsity-alone. Quality: ~98.4% Open-LLM-Leaderboard-v1 recovery (~1.6% avg gap) is REAL but gated on heavy co-design.
assessment.delivery: Host a co-designed checkpoint (FEASIBLE, exactly like CIPHER hosts a quant). The Sparse-Llama checkpoints are public (RedHatAI/neuralmagic on HuggingFace) in compressed-tensors format and already deploy under unmodified vLLM, which CIPHER interposes. CIPHER would NOT and CANNOT invent it: recovering quality required 45 BILLION tokens of sparse continued-pretraining + knowledge distillation for Llama-2-7B (13B tokens for the newer 3.1-8B), ~26 GPU-hours-class jobs on 32 H100s — that is the 'needs-finetune' model-side work the founding research lacked, and it is out of scope for a driver-interposition substrate to produce. So: ship-by-hosting yes; create-the-structure no.
assessment.reasoning: This is the ONE lever that differs structurally from the founding failures: 2:4 is hardware-accelerated (Sparse Tensor Cores, 2x peak FLOPs), so unlike Monarch/Koopman/activation-sparsity it does not merely lower the FLOP numerator — it CAN raise tokens/sec. And co-design fixes the founding's fatal flaw: post-hoc one-shot SparseGPT recovers only ~77% (MMLU 0.667->0.404), the same post-hoc collapse the founding saw; freezing the mask and continued-pretraining on 45B tokens restores quality to 96-98%. So the verdict is NOT 'overstated', 'quality-killer', or 'flop-reduction-not-throughput'. BUT it is also NOT 'real-2x-hardware': the 2x peak never materializes on real 7B layers at H100 because (1) decode is memory-bound and dense H100 cuBLAS is already near-optimal, (2) decompression/metadata overhead dominates at the small M typical of LLM linear layers, and (3) independent reproductions (PyTorch #153825: 0.37-0.67x slower; SlideSparse 1.34-1.5x large-M-only; cuSPARSELt ~1.6x) bound the real win to ~1.1-1.3x and only in large-batch prefill. Net: a genuine but modest, regime-dependent hardware speedup whose quality preservation REQUIRES large-scale finetune — hence 'real-but-needs-finetune'. CIPHER can legitimately ship this by hosting the public co-designed checkpoint; it cannot manufacture the checkpoint. Sources: Red Hat Developer (2025-02-28, 2024-12-18) for vendor speed/quality; arXiv:2405.03594 for one-shot-77%/96.1%-after-45B-tokens; PyTorch issue #153825 and SlideSparse arXiv:2603.05232 and HPC-AI blog for adversarial H100 reproductions showing sub-1.0x at realistic 7B shapes.

assessment.method: 2:4 Sparse Llama-2-7B + FP8 (sparse-FP8 CUTLASS) on H100 — stacking 2:4 weight sparsity (Sparse Tensor Cores, 2x peak) with FP8 weights/activations, co-designed via sparse pretraining + calibration.
assessment.honest_gain: Real, hardware-accelerated, but the gain is mostly FP8 — not sparsity. Vendor (Neural Magic/Red Hat) measured on H100: 1.7x lower single-stream latency, 1.5x higher multi-stream throughput vs dense BF16 — but explicitly only "up to 30% of latency / up to 20% of throughput gains attributed to sparsity alone." So the 2:4 sparsity lever itself contributes ~1.2-1.3x; FP8 supplies the rest. GEMM-kernel level (the favorable, isolated number): FP8 alone up to 1.9x over BF16; FP8+2:4 up to 2.5x over BF16; sparse-FP8 GEMM only 1.22x over DENSE FP8. Honest expected gain for H100/7B-dense/quality-preserved attributable to the 2:4 lever: ~1.2-1.3x end-to-end on top of FP8, and that increment is largest in memory-bound decode (byte reduction), not a clean 2x compute win. Two honesty flags on the source claim: (a) the headline E2E benchmark is Llama-3.1-8B at batch=1, NOT Llama-2-7B; (b) "1.5x throughput" is at batch=1 single-stream multiplexing, not a saturated high-batch serving throughput — at large prefill batches Sparse-Marlin-class kernels are ~10% SLOWER than dense (compute-bound, sparsity adds metadata overhead). This is NOT flop-reduction-not-throughput: 2:4 runs on real Sparse Tensor Cores (2x peak silicon), so it does raise tokens/sec at fixed quality, unlike the founding's post-hoc low-rank/Monarch attempts that only cut FLOPs.
assessment.delivery: CIPHER ships this by HOSTING a co-designed checkpoint, exactly as it hosts a quantized one — feasible. CIPHER CANNOT create the checkpoint: quality recovery required 45B tokens of sparse PRETRAINING on SlimPajama+Stack (2-8% of Llama-2's original 2T tokens) plus task fine-tuning. One-shot SparseGPT (no retrain) is insufficient and "unstable at 70% sparsity"; only at 50% with full sparse-pretrain + fine-tune do you reach 96.1% foundational recovery and "full recovery on average" after task FT. So "needs-finetune" UNDERSTATES it — it needs sparse pretraining, a model-team/GPU-cluster job, fully outside CIPHER's driver-interposition surface. CIPHER's role: serve the published Neural Magic 2:4-sparse-FP8 checkpoint via sparse-FP8 CUTLASS kernels under unmodified vLLM (kernels already exist in vLLM/LLM-Compressor). Net for CIPHER as a SUBSTRATE: the deliverable lever is FP8 (which CIPHER already evidenced internally as throughput+power, not MFU) plus a modest ~1.2-1.3x decode increment IF and only IF an externally-co-designed 2:4 checkpoint is dropped in. CIPHER invents nothing here; it is a hosting target.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification against the four required tests. (1) REAL on H100, not paper-FLOP? YES — 2:4 uses Sparse Tensor Cores with 2x peak silicon, confirmed by NVIDIA/PyTorch and the Sparse-Marlin kernel (near-2x decode over dense FP16, ~5.3x as a 4-bit+2:4 stack on A100). This is a genuine tokens/sec raise, distinguishing it from the founding's low-rank/Monarch failures which only lowered the FLOP numerator. (2) Quality cost honest? The vendor says "near-full accuracy recovery" with NO single percentage on GSM8K/HumanEval/AlpacaEval in the FP8 article — soft. The underlying paper (arXiv 2405.03594) is honest: 96.1% recovery at 50% / 91.8% at 70% foundational, full recovery only after task FT, and one-shot pruning explicitly insufficient. So quality IS preserved but ONLY with heavy retraining; the "needs-finetune" tag is correct directionally but should read "needs sparse pretraining (45B tokens)." (3) What CIPHER ships? Host a co-designed checkpoint (feasible, like quant) — it cannot invent the structure. (4) Honest gain: the sparsity-attributable increment is ~1.2-1.3x E2E, concentrated in memory-bound decode; the rest is FP8. Skeptical caveats found: headline benchmark is 3.1-8B@batch=1 not 2-7B; "throughput" is single-stream-multiplex not saturated-batch; at high prefill batch sparse kernels go ~10% slower; w4a16+2:4 ≈ w4a16 alone in one independent report (minimal extra benefit). Verdict real-but-needs-finetune: the speedup is hardware-real and quality is recoverable, but the recovery work is a large external pretraining job CIPHER cannot perform, and the portion of the win uniquely owed to the 2:4 lever (vs FP8 alone, which CIPHER already has) is modest. Sources: developers.redhat.com/articles/2024/12/18 (FP8+2:4 SOTA Hopper), arxiv.org/abs/2405.03594 (Sparse Llama pretraining), github.com/IST-DASLab/Sparse-Marlin, docs.vllm.ai LLM-Compressor 2of4+w4a16. All numbers vendor-reported; no independent H100 reproduction of the exact 1.7x/1.5x was found, so treat headline E2E figures as vendor-measured-not-independently-reproduced.

assessment.method: Sparse-Marlin (2:4 structured sparsity + W4A16 INT4) GEMM kernel in vLLM, for H100 / 7B-dense (Mistral/Llama).
assessment.honest_gain: Honest H100/7B-dense, quality-preserved, END-TO-END: ~1.2-1.35x throughput vs an FP16 dense baseline, and effectively NEUTRAL-to-marginal (~1.0-1.2x) vs a CIPHER baseline that already runs W4A16/FP8 — because most of the win is the 4-bit weight traffic CIPHER already captures (the founding's own W4A16 Marlin lever), and the 2:4 sparse-tensor-core compute path only adds value in the compute-bound high-batch prefill regime, not in memory-bound decode. The flashy numbers do NOT survive scrutiny for H100: Sparse-Marlin's '5.3x vs dense Marlin', '+65%', '3.3x on A6000' are Ampere kernel microbenchmarks (RTX 3090 / A10 / A6000) at near-ideal small batch (16-32). The Marlin authors themselves state Hopper portability is 'untested and non-trivial', and H100 has NO native INT4 tensor core (A100 does) — the INT4 path is not Hopper's natural math (FP8 is). The honest measured H100/H200 end-to-end for 2:4+low-precision is 1.27x (Llama-3-8B sparse+FP8, 123.66s->97.64s) and ~1.33x (Llama-2-70B, NVIDIA), far below the 2x sparse-TC peak because non-GEMM ops (softmax/norm/KV I/O) and memory-bound decode don't shrink.
assessment.delivery: CIPHER ships this by HOSTING a co-designed checkpoint (feasible — identical to how it already hosts a quantized model; LLMCompressor produces the 2:4+W4A16 artifact and vLLM has the kernel for capability>8.0 incl. Hopper). CIPHER CANNOT invent the structure: the checkpoint must be pre-built with real model-side work. Required model-side work is substantial and non-negotiable for quality: post-hoc 2:4 is a quality-killer (SparseGPT one-shot on Llama-2-7B: PPL 7.26->13.54; MMLU 5-shot 0.667->0.404). Recovery to ~96-98% of dense needs EITHER sparse pretraining (Neural Magic: 45B tokens for 50% sparse, 100B for 70%; ~2-8% of original 2T-token budget) OR at minimum one epoch of recovery finetuning + GPTQ calibration (official vLLM/LLMCompressor recipe, which warns 'fine tuning can require more steps than shown'). This is exactly the founding's POST-HOC failure resolved by CO-DESIGN — but the co-design cost lands on whoever produces the checkpoint, not on CIPHER's interposition layer.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification resolved four ways. (1) Is the speedup REAL on H100, not paper-FLOP? PARTIALLY. The 2:4 sparse-tensor-core path IS hardware-accelerated (raises tokens/sec at fixed quality, unlike pure FLOP-reduction) — this is the one structure on the list that touches a 2x-peak hardware path, so it is qualitatively better than Monarch/Koopman/SwiGLU-sparsity which only cut the FLOP numerator. BUT the realized H100 end-to-end is 1.27-1.35x, not the headline 1.5-5.3x: those are Ampere microbenchmarks at ideal batch, and the kernel was authored for Ampere wgmma-less paths (Hopper port untested per authors; no native H100 INT4). (2) Is quality cost honest? The CLAIM ('minimal degradation', '~98% recovery') is honest ONLY conditioned on the underlying finetuned sparse checkpoint — which the method card correctly flags as 'needs-finetune'. Stripped of finetune it is a quality-killer (MMLU 0.667->0.404). So 'minimal degradation' is true-with-an-asterisk: it imports 45B-token recovery cost. (3) What would CIPHER ship? Hosting a co-designed checkpoint is feasible (= quant-hosting). Inventing it is infeasible. Verdict 'real-but-needs-finetune' over 'flop-reduction-not-throughput' because the 2:4 path genuinely raises throughput on real hardware (not just FLOPs), and over 'overstated' because the core claim is real once you accept the finetune precondition — but the headline multipliers ARE overstated for H100. (4) Honest gain for H100/7B-dense/preserved-quality: ~1.2-1.35x vs FP16 dense, shrinking toward neutral against CIPHER's existing 4-bit baseline since the marginal 2:4 win over already-quantized weights is the compute path only, which is dormant in memory-bound 7B decode (the founding's own W4A16 finding: 'fires at M=1, kernel already cutlass/marlin-optimal'). Net: a real but modest, finetune-gated lever; best case is the customer brings a 2:4+W4A16 checkpoint and CIPHER hosts it for an incremental prefill/high-batch gain. Sources: IST-DASLab/Sparse-Marlin (github), MARLIN arXiv:2408.11743, Neural Magic Sparse-Llama arXiv:2405.03594 (45B tokens, 96.1% recovery, 1.7x A10), hpc-ai.com 2:4+FP8 blog (1.27x H-class, MMLU 0.404->0.604 with finetune), vLLM/LLMCompressor 2of4_sparse_w4a16 docs (recovery finetune + GPTQ), SparseGPT 2:4 PPL 7.26->13.54.

research.summary: DIRECT ANSWER TO KEY QUESTION: Yes — the founding's failure was specifically *naive, uniform, post-hoc full-layer rank-k* (no activation weighting, one global rank, no recovery), which gave KL=13 mode-collapse. 2024-2025 SOTA fixes this WITHOUT retraining, using two cheap model-side tricks that are still post-hoc/calibration-only: (1) ACTIVATION-AWARE WHITENING — scale weights by an activation covariance (Cholesky of XXᵀ) before SVD so truncation minimizes OUTPUT error, not weight error (SVD-LLM, ASVD, Basis-Sharing, FLAT-LLM); (2) PER-LAYER / TRUNCATION-AWARE RANK ALLOCATION instead of one global rank (Fisher/sensitivity-driven). These recover most of the quality the founding lost. BUT BRUTAL HONESTY ON THE TRADE: on a 7B, even SOTA degrades meaningfully — LLaMA-7B WikiText-2 baseline PPL 5.68 goes to ~7.7 at 20% compression (SVD-LLM/Basis-Sharing) and ~9-15 at 40-60%. There is NO free-lunch lossless 7B low-rank; the dense 7B is close to full-rank (consistent with the founding's 23/32 full-rank finding). Adding optional LoRA recovery helps but crosses into light-finetune territory.\n\nMFU/THROUGHPUT VERDICT (the crux for CIPHER): low-rank is FUNDAMENTALLY DIFFERENT from unstructured pruning on the FLOP-vs-hardware axis. It replaces one dense W (m×n) with two SMALLER DENSE GEMMs (m×k and k×n), k<<min(m,n). Those are ordinary dense GEMMs that run on the SAME tensor cores at full efficiency — NO special sparse hardware, NO 2:4 pattern, NO custom kernel needed for the math to map to MFU. It reduces BOTH weight-bytes AND FLOPs. Therefore: at MEMORY-BOUND DECODE (CIPHER's batch=1/low-batch regime) it gives a REAL tokens/sec gain because fewer weight bytes are read per token (exactly like quantization helps decode) — this is the opposite of the 'FLOP reduction lowers numerator with no speedup' trap. At COMPUTE-BOUND PREFILL it gives a real gain because the GEMM is genuinely smaller. Measured A100 throughput: SVD-LLM 1.2x@20% / 1.7x@40% / 2.1x@60%; Basis-Sharing 1.57x@50% (batch512); Dobi-SVD 1.75x@40% (A100, honest number). CAVEATS THAT BITE: (a) the eye-popping '12.4x' (Dobi-SVD) is a memory-FIT artifact on a 12GB Titan Xp where the uncompressed model spills/swaps — NOT a compute speedup; the A100 ~1.75x is the real number. (b) FlashSVD shows naive SVD does NOT reduce PEAK inference memory because activation buffers still materialize at full size unless you fuse the two factors with a custom kernel — so the memory win needs a fused U·V kernel, which is exactly the kind of thing CIPHER's GEMM-interception layer would host. (c) two thin GEMMs have lower per-GEMM arithmetic intensity than one fat GEMM and add a kernel launch, so realized speedup < FLOP-ratio at low compression. FIT FOR CIPHER: low-rank maps cleanly onto CIPHER's 'host a modified checkpoint like a quantized one' model — the factorization is done offline with calibration (no retrain), and CIPHER intercepts the GEMM and runs W≈U·V (ideally a fused kernel). It is post-hoc/light-calibration, hardware-friendly (dense tensor cores), and unlike the founding's failure it actually preserves quality up to ~20-30% compression. The catch vs the founding's hope: it's a lossy compression knob (a few PPL points), not a lossless free speedup.

methods.name: SVD-LLM (truncation-aware whitened SVD + optional LoRA) — ICLR 2025
methods.math: Whiten W by Cholesky factor S of activation Gram (XXᵀ): truncate singular values of W·S so that dropping σ_i minimizes OUTPUT reconstruction error ‖ΔW·X‖ (not ‖ΔW‖). Replace dense W (m×n) with two dense GEMMs U(m×k)·V(k×n). Optional sequential low-rank + LoRA-style parameter update on 50K Alpaca samples for recovery.
methods.measured_speedup: A100 GPU end-to-end generation throughput: 1.2x @20% compression, 1.7x @40%, 2.1x @60%, 3.1x @80%. Two dense GEMMs run on standard tensor cores (no special hardware). Gain grows with batch size / shorter sequences. SVD-LLM V2: 1.29x/1.63x/2.08x/2.71x at same ratios.
methods.measured_quality: LLaMA-7B WikiText-2 PPL: baseline 5.68 → 7.73 @20% → 9.27 @40% → 15.00 @60%. Quality degrades steadily; usable mainly ≤20-40% on a 7B. ~99% PPL reduction vs naive SVD baselines at ≥40% (i.e. it rescues the founding's collapse but is still lossy).
methods.posthoc_possible: YES post-hoc — needs 256 WikiText calibration samples to compute the activation whitening matrix; NO weight retraining required for the core method. LoRA recovery (50K Alpaca samples) is OPTIONAL and pushes into light-finetune for the last bit of quality.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA A100 (paper). Math is two dense GEMMs → maps to standard tensor cores at full MFU; no 2:4/sparse hardware needed. Memory-bound decode benefits from reduced weight-byte reads (like quantization).

methods.name: ASVD — Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition (training-free)
methods.math: Transform W by a diagonal activation-distribution scaling so activation outliers are absorbed into the weight before SVD, improving low-rank decomposition accuracy; iterative per-layer sensitivity calibration assigns truncation rank per layer (Sensitivity-based Truncation Rank Search).
methods.measured_speedup: Not the headline contribution — ASVD targets size/KV reduction; reports 10-30% model-size compression and ~50% KV-cache memory reduction. Throughput speedup modest and not the central claim (memory-oriented).
methods.measured_quality: Quality holds for mild compression but PPL rises rapidly below ~0.85 parameter-ratio (i.e. >15% compression) as sensitive layers lose rank — confirms 7B is near-full-rank and aggressive low-rank is lossy even with activation-awareness.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES — fully training-free / post-hoc; uses a calibration set only to estimate activation scaling and per-layer sensitivity. No finetune.
methods.hardware: GPU (A100-class in paper). Dense factor GEMMs; KV-cache low-rank reduces attention memory bandwidth.

methods.name: Basis Sharing — cross-layer shared basis SVD (ICLR 2025)
methods.math: Decompose each layer's whitened weight as a linear combination of a SET of basis vectors SHARED across layers plus per-layer coefficients, so basis storage is amortized across layers; activation-aware whitening as in SVD-LLM. Still two dense GEMMs at inference per layer.
methods.measured_speedup: 1.57x throughput vs dense at 50% compression on single A100 (batch 512, seq 32). Standard dense GEMMs.
methods.measured_quality: LLaMA-7B WikiText-2 PPL: 7.74 @20%, 12.39 @40%, 19.99 @50% (baseline 5.68). Beats SVD-LLM at equal ratio (e.g. 19.99 vs 23.97 @50%, ~15.8% lower PPL) — current SVD SOTA for quality-at-ratio, but still clearly lossy on 7B.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES post-hoc — 256 WikiText calibration samples for the scaling matrix; NO finetune for zero-shot eval; LoRA optional for recovery.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA A100. Dense tensor-core GEMMs; no special sparse hardware.

methods.name: Dobi-SVD — differentiable truncation-position SVD (ICLR 2025)
methods.math: Make the truncation rank per layer a DIFFERENTIABLE parameter; train only the truncation positions (224 params for LLaMA-7B, ~8 GPU-hrs, 16 calib samples) via straight-through on activations, then rebuild optimal weights via incremental PCA. Inference = two dense factor GEMMs.
methods.measured_speedup: A100 80GB: up to 1.75x @40% compression (HONEST compute number). Titan Xp 12GB: '12.4x' / 25.97 tok/s — but this is a MEMORY-FIT artifact (uncompressed model spills VRAM and swaps), NOT a compute speedup; do not cite as real GPU throughput gain.
methods.measured_quality: LLaMA-7B WikiText-2 PPL: ~9.07-9.95 @40%, 8.12 @60%, 6.08 @80% (note: their ratio convention may differ; paper claims ~78.7% PPL improvement over prior SVD SOTA at 40%). Best-in-class quality-at-ratio among SVD methods, but still ~+3-4 PPL over the 5.68 baseline at 40%.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES — calibration-only; trains only 224 truncation-position scalars (8 GPU-hrs), not the weights. No full finetune.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (real speedup) and Titan Xp 12GB (memory-fit speedup — discount). Dense factor GEMMs on tensor cores.

methods.name: Palu — low-rank KV-cache compression (ICLR 2025)
methods.math: SVD-decompose the K/V projection weights; cache the small LOW-RANK latent states instead of full K/V and reconstruct on-the-fly; grouped (medium-grained) decomposition + Fisher-based rank search + low-rank-aware quantization + fused reconstruction kernel. Reduces KV-cache memory bandwidth in attention.
methods.measured_speedup: Up to 1.61x end-to-end attention-module speedup at 50% KV compression; up to 2.48x GEMV reconstruction speedup (75% key compression, M-LRD) at 16K context; up to 2.91x attention when combined with quantization. Speedup is from BOTH reduced KV memory bandwidth (memory-bound long-context decode) AND reduced reconstruction FLOPs (compute-bound at long seq).
methods.measured_quality: Llama2-7B: PPL 5.63 @50% low-rank (baseline 5.47), ~2.4% zero-shot accuracy drop (G-LRD g=4). With 2-bit quant: 91.25% KV compression, PPL 6.41 (beats KVQuant by 1.19 PPL).
methods.posthoc_possible: YES — post-training SVD on frozen weights with Fisher-info rank allocation; NO calibration finetune, NO retrain. Orthogonal to weight-GEMM low-rank: this is the KV-cache / long-context lever specifically.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA A6000 (paper). Custom fused reconstruction GPU kernel; benefits long-context decode which is KV-bandwidth-bound — directly relevant to CIPHER decode regime.

methods.name: FlashSVD — fused low-rank inference kernel (caveat/enabler, 2025)
methods.math: Stream the two low-rank factors U,V through a FUSED kernel so the full-size intermediate activation X·U·V is never materialized; tiles the rank dimension to keep activations on-chip. Addresses the gap that naive SVD inference still allocates full-width activation buffers.
methods.measured_speedup: FFN module 1.9x over dense at rank 96; long-context attention 1.64x over FlashAttention at rank 16; ~20% faster end-to-end vs vanilla SVD at 50% compression. KEY CAVEAT IT EXPOSES: WITHOUT a fused kernel, naive SVD achieves ZERO peak-inference-memory reduction (activations dominate); peak-memory win (up to 70.2% on BERT-Base, 75% transient) requires this fused implementation.
methods.measured_quality: Lossless relative to the upstream low-rank model (≤0.58% variance) — it is an inference-kernel method, not a new compression; quality = whatever compression feeds it.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES — pure inference-time kernel; takes an already-factorized model. CRITICAL FOR CIPHER: this is the kernel CIPHER would need to host the U·V product as a fused GEMM to realize the memory + speed win rather than just FLOP-on-paper.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA L40S (paper); principle generalizes to H100. Demonstrates low-rank delivers BOTH weight reduction AND inference speedup only when factors are fused (custom kernel) — the integration point for a GEMM-interception substrate.

assessment.method: SVD-LLM (ICLR 2025) + SVD-LLM V2 (NAACL 2025): truncation-aware whitened SVD. Whiten W by Cholesky factor S of the activation Gram XX^T, truncate singular values of W*S to minimize output error norm(dW*X), replace dense W (m x n) with two dense GEMMs U(m x k)*V(k x n). Optional sequential low-rank + LoRA-style update on 50K Alpaca samples. Calibration = 256 WikiText-2 samples. Post-training only; NO from-scratch retrain. Runs on standard tensor cores (two dense GEMMs), no special hardware.
assessment.honest_gain: For H100 / 7B-dense / batch=1 decode at PRESERVED quality (~20-30% compression where PPL is still tolerable): expect roughly 1.0-1.2x tokens/sec at best, likely under 1.1x and possibly no gain or a slowdown. The headline 1.2x@20% / 2.1x@60% (V2: 1.29/1.63/2.08/2.71x) are A100, prefill-heavy numbers (V2 measured at batch=4, prefill=1024, decode=256 = compute-bound), NOT the batch=1 memory-bound decode where CIPHER serves. Quality caps usable compression at ~20-40% on a 7B: WikiText-2 PPL 5.68 -> 7.73 (+36%) @20%, -> 9.27 @40% even WITH the 50K-Alpaca LoRA recovery; zero-shot avg 0.57 -> 0.55 @20% / 0.50 @40%. The 2-3x figures live at 60-80% where quality collapses (PPL 15.0 / 31.8). At the modest rank cuts that preserve quality the throughput gain is marginal-to-negative.
assessment.delivery: HOST a co-designed checkpoint -- FEASIBLE, exactly like hosting a quantized model. CIPHER invents/retrains nothing: the model owner runs SVD-LLM whitening + (needed past ~20%) the 50K-Alpaca LoRA recovery offline to produce factored weights; CIPHER intercepts each linear and issues TWO dense cuBLAS/cutlass GEMMs (U then V) on standard tensor cores instead of one. No special hardware, no kernel CIPHER lacks -- squarely within the 'host a modified checkpoint like a quantized one' charter. What is INFEASIBLE is imposing this post-hoc on a frozen model and keeping quality (the founding's exact failure): whitening-only ('W' variant) still collapses (PPL 66.6 @60%, 1349 @80%); the rescue past 20% requires the provider's calibration+LoRA step. So delivery requires model-side work (calibration always; light finetune past ~20%) done by the checkpoint provider, not by CIPHER.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification across 6 sources. (1) Real on hardware or paper-FLOP? Real but regime-limited and standard-tensor-core only. Break-even is decisive: two GEMMs cost 2k(m+n) vs dense mn, so FLOPs drop only when k < mn/(m+n); for square LLM matrices (m~n~d) that is k < d/2 -- you must truncate MORE than half the rank before the factored form even has fewer FLOPs than dense. '20% compression' = 20% PARAMETER reduction via a modest rank cut, so FLOP reduction at preserved quality is small. And it is NOT hardware-accelerated structure: unlike 2:4 sparsity (per SliceGPT/SparseGPT lit, the only scheme that hits sparse tensor cores for ~2x peak), SVD-LLM runs two DENSE GEMMs -- it lowers the FLOP numerator, it does not raise peak throughput. (2) Quality cost honest? Yes and modest: PPL +36% @20% even with LoRA; it rescues naive-SVD collapse (~99% PPL reduction vs vanilla SVD at >=40%) but stays lossy, and the preservation REQUIRES the calibration+LoRA co-design (whitening-only collapses). This genuinely beats the founding's frozen post-hoc Koopman (KL=13 mode-collapse) -- but only by adding the recovery finetune. (3) FLOP-vs-throughput at CIPHER's regime: authors state speedup grows with batch size and shrinks with sequence length, V2 measured at batch=4/prefill=1024 (compute-bound). CIPHER's 7B target is batch=1 decode = memory-bound (your own MFU work: decode MFU 0.2-23%). There two GEMMs add HBM<->SRAM round-trips and parallelization inefficiency. Independent corroboration: FlashSVD (L40S) measured naive-SVD latency at 50% compression = 150.8ms = identical to dense, fused only 6.1% faster, and naive low-rank does not even reduce peak memory (intermediate Vx must be materialized); SliceGPT got 1.11x @25% on 7B and 10% extra memory @20% on Llama-2-7B. The headline curve does not transfer to single-stream decode. (4) Ship: hosting a factored checkpoint is feasible (two cuBLAS calls, std tensor cores); the infeasible part is quality-preserving structure without the provider's offline calibration+finetune. Bottom line: a real method that beats the founding's frozen-SVD failure, but for H100/7B/preserved-quality/decode it is FLOP-reduction that does not reliably raise tokens/sec. Sources: SVD-LLM arxiv 2403.07378 (PPL 7.73/9.27/15.00/31.79 @20/40/60/80, zero-shot 0.55/0.50, A100, 256-sample calib + 50K Alpaca); SVD-LLM V2 arxiv 2503.12340 (1.29/1.63/2.08/2.71x @ batch=4/prefill=1024/decode=256, PPL 7.12 @20%); FlashSVD arxiv 2508.01506 (naive SVD 150.8ms=dense @50%, +6.1% fused, no peak-mem saving, L40S); SliceGPT arxiv 2401.15024 (1.11x @25% 7B; 2:4 = only scheme hitting sparse tensor cores); break-even r < d_in*d_out/(d_in+d_out) confirmed across multiple low-rank-GEMM papers.

assessment.method: ASVD — Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition (training-free low-rank weight compression). Absorbs activation outliers into W via diagonal activation-magnitude scaling before SVD, then assigns per-layer truncation rank via Sensitivity-based Truncation Rank Search (STRS). Replaces each W·x GEMM with two smaller matmuls (U·Σ)·(Vᵀ·x). Calibration only (~32×2048 ≈ 65K tokens, no gradient/finetune).
assessment.honest_gain: For H100 / 7B-dense / quality preserved (PPL within a few %): NEAR-ZERO real tokens/sec gain. ASVD itself reports NO throughput number — its headline is 10-30% size and ~50% KV-cache memory reduction, not speed. The quality-preserving compression band is tiny: LLaMA-7B Wiki PPL 5.68(1.0)→6.09(0.9,+7%)→6.80(0.85,+20%); the paper's own line is "below 0.85 param ratio, rapid increase in PPL," and an independent critique shows ASVD blowing up to PPL 1407 at 0.6. The successor SVD-LLM reports its MAX 1.7x ONLY at 40% compression where LLaMA-7B PPL = 13.11 (2.3x baseline = quality destroyed), and only on A100, not H100; at a genuinely quality-safe 20% compression PPL is already 7.94 (+40%) for a sub-1.2x best case. Crucially the speedup is pure FLOP reduction via two smaller matmuls — NO hardware-accelerated structure. Multiple sources flag that splitting one GEMM into two "degrades GPU efficiency," is "very implementation-sensitive," adds kernel launches/unfavorable shapes, and adds activation-memory overhead that standard dense kernels can't reclaim (FlashSVD exists specifically to patch this). On 7B-dense H100 decode (memory-bound, MFU 0.2-23% per CIPHER's own founding measurements), shaving the FLOP numerator does not move the memory-bound bottleneck. Honest expected gain at preserved quality: effectively 1.0x throughput; the only real win is a MEMORY win (~50% KV-cache, modest weight-size), not a tokens/sec win. Contrast: 2:4 structured sparsity is the only post-hoc structure that DOES raise H100 throughput (real 1.27-1.83x via sparse tensor cores = 2x peak) — but it mandates 50% prune that collapses quality (Qwen3 54%→15%) and needs finetune to recover.
assessment.delivery: HOST (feasible, like a quant checkpoint) — NOT invent. ASVD is training-free / light-calibration-only, so a co-designed ASVD checkpoint can be produced offline and CIPHER could host the decomposed (U·Σ, Vᵀ) factors as two GEMMs under unmodified vLLM, exactly the way it hosts a quantized checkpoint. No retrain required, so the model-side work is feasible. BUT delivery is a trap for CIPHER's actual goal (raise tokens/sec at fixed quality): hosting the checkpoint is easy; the throughput payoff isn't there. Two smaller cuBLAS/cutlass GEMMs at quality-safe rank are not hardware-accelerated and stay memory-bound at decode — CIPHER would be hosting a memory-footprint optimization mislabeled as a compute speedup. If CIPHER wants the memory/KV win, ASVD is a feasible host; if it wants tokens/sec at preserved quality, this lever does not deliver and the FLOP reduction is too small (≤10-15% compression) to overcome split-GEMM inefficiency.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification across 4 checks. (1) Speedup REAL on H100? NO — ASVD reports zero throughput numbers; the strongest successor (SVD-LLM) reports 1.7x only on A100 and only at 40% compression where quality is destroyed; mechanism is two-smaller-matmuls FLOP reduction with no sparse-tensor-core acceleration, and independent sources confirm split GEMMs "degrade GPU efficiency" and are "implementation-sensitive." This is paper-FLOP reduction, not a tokens/sec raise, and it does not touch the memory-bound decode bottleneck that dominates 7B H100 serving. (2) Quality cost honest? The method is genuinely post-hoc/training-free (good), but the quality envelope is narrow and the paper admits it: rapid PPL rise below 0.85 param ratio, catastrophic failure (PPL 1000+) at 0.6. This directly CONFIRMS CIPHER's founding finding that 7B is near-full-rank and aggressive low-rank is lossy — activation-awareness only buys a few % more compression, not a regime change. (3) Ship = host or invent? Host is feasible (training-free checkpoint, quant-like), so no infeasible model invention is required — but the throughput goal isn't met by hosting it. (4) Honest gain at preserved quality on H100/7B-dense: ~1.0x tokens/sec (memory/KV win only). Verdict flop-reduction-not-throughput rather than quality-killer because at the conservative ranks that DO preserve quality there's no quality cliff — there's just no speed; the quality cliff only appears if you push compression hard enough to chase a speedup, which then kills quality. The honest takeaway for CIPHER: ASVD validates that co-designed low-rank still can't beat the near-full-rank wall for throughput; only hardware-accelerated structure (2:4) raises H100 tokens/sec, and that path has its own quality/finetune problem.

assessment.method: Basis Sharing — cross-layer shared-basis SVD (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2410.03765). Each layer's activation-whitened (SVD-LLM-style) weight W is approximated as B''·C': a basis matrix B'' shared across a group of layers plus per-layer coefficients C'. K/Q/V/Up/Gate share bases; O/Down use per-layer SVD. Inference = two sequential STANDARD DENSE GEMMs per weight (input·B''·C'). Calibration-only (256 WikiText-2 samples × 2048 tok to estimate the whitening matrix); no fine-tuning for headline numbers.
assessment.honest_gain: For H100 / 7B-dense / PRESERVED quality: ~1.1–1.25x prefill/compute-bound throughput at best, and effectively NO honest win at decode batch=1. The paper's headline 1.57x @50% is REAL but (a) measured on A100, (b) at batch=512/seq=32 (a compute-bound prefill-like regime where halving GEMM FLOPs directly helps), and (c) at a 50% ratio whose quality is destroyed (WikiText-2 PPL 5.68→19.99, ~3.5x worse). At a quality-PRESERVING ratio (~20%, PPL 7.74, still +36% PPL and not free), the FLOP cut is only ~20%, so realistic compute-bound speedup is ~1.1–1.2x and decode (memory-bound, the dominant serving cost) sees roughly proportional weight-load reduction only at large batch. This is FLOP/byte reduction on dense GEMMs, NOT hardware-accelerated structure: there is no 2:4 sparse tensor-core path, so peak FLOPs are not doubled and nothing raises tokens/sec at FIXED quality the way 2:4 sparsity does. Corroborated by SVD-LLM V2's own throughput table (1.29x@20%, 1.63x@40%, 2.08x@60% on A100 batch=4) — speedup scales with compression ratio, i.e. with how much quality you are willing to burn.
assessment.delivery: HOST a co-designed checkpoint — feasible, exactly like hosting a quantized model. The factored weights B''·C' are just two dense GEMMs per layer, so CIPHER's cuBLAS/cutlass interposition hosts them under unmodified vLLM with no retrain, identical to the W4A16/quant hosting pattern. CIPHER does NOT and cannot invent the decomposition: producing B''/C' is an offline model-side step (activation whitening + grouped SVD + rank allocation). But that step is LIGHT — calibration-only, 256 samples, A100-minutes — not a training run. CAVEAT: to keep quality acceptable at useful ratios, SOTA in this family (SVD-LLM V2, Prehab-SVD) adds a LoRA recovery fine-tune; the calibration-only Basis Sharing numbers are the lossy floor, so a deployable quality-preserving checkpoint likely needs a light LoRA pass (still cheap, but no longer zero model-side work).
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification across 5 searches + 2 source fetches: (1) SPEED REAL BUT REGIME-GAMED: 1.57x is genuine on A100 but at batch=512/seq=32 — the compute-bound regime where FLOP cuts pay off. CIPHER's own prior work shows 7B decode is memory-bound (MFU 0.2-23%); a low-rank GEMM there saves weight-load bytes only at large batch and never doubles peak like 2:4 tensor cores. No hardware-accelerated structure is involved — standard dense GEMMs, so this is the classic 'lower the numerator' lever, not a tokens/sec-at-fixed-quality win. (2) QUALITY COST HONEST AND LOSSY: calibration-only is genuinely no-retrain, but PPL@50%=19.99 is a quality-killer and even @20%=7.74 is +36% over the 5.68 baseline — not preserved. Basis Sharing beats SVD-LLM (19.99 vs 23.97) so it IS current quality-at-ratio SOTA for pure-SVD, but 'best lossy' is still lossy on 7B. The direct critique paper (Cross-Layer Subspace Coupling: Empirical Limits, arXiv 2605.30836) proves the cross-layer shared-basis idea wins on Frobenius reconstruction yet that does NOT transfer to perplexity (3.2x PPL blow-up in their untied variant on Pythia-1.4B) and explicitly declines to verify at Llama/7B scale — so the cross-layer-sharing benefit over per-layer SVD is fragile and unvalidated at 7B. (3) FINETUNE REALITY: the SOTA descendants (SVD-LLM V2, Prehab-SVD) all add LoRA recovery to make ratios usable, confirming calibration-only hits a quality wall. (4) This is NOT the founding's post-hoc failure repeated: it is co-designed (whitening + grouped SVD chooses structure with calibration data), which is why it produces ANY working compression where post-hoc Monarch/Koopman gave KL=13 collapse. Net: a feasible-to-host, light-model-side-work lever whose honest H100/7B/quality-preserving payoff is modest (~1.1-1.2x compute-bound, ~nil decode-bound) and far below the headline because the headline trades quality for FLOPs and runs in a compute-bound batch regime. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2410.03765 (Basis Sharing), arxiv.org/pdf/2403.07378 (SVD-LLM), arxiv.org/pdf/2503.12340 (SVD-LLM V2 throughput table), arxiv.org/html/2605.30836 (Empirical Limits critique), arxiv.org/pdf/2508.01506 (FlashSVD activation-overhead critique).

research.summary:
DIRECT ANSWER TO KEY QUESTION: Yes — co-design reverses the founding's post-hoc failure on the QUALITY axis. When structure is TRAINED IN (pretrain from scratch, or fine-tune-after-projection), Monarch/BTT/structured-FFN reach dense-parity quality at 25-70% of the parameters/FLOPs — exactly where the frozen-model Monarch/Koopman/sparsity probes collapsed (KL=13 mode-collapse, 9/32 layers). BTT matches dense ViT-S/32 at 3.8x less COMPUTE; structured-FFN trained-in at 32% of FFN params loses only ~0.4-1.0 perplexity (self-guided training closes most of the gap); Monarch trains GPT-2/ViT 2x faster at "comparable quality." SO co-design is real and these are genuine results.

BUT THE BRUTAL HONESTY FOR CIPHER: the speedup is overwhelmingly a TRAINING-FLOP / parameter-count win, NOT a fixed-quality inference tokens/sec win on an H100. Three independent 2024-2026 systems papers measure that FLOP reduction does NOT translate to GPU wall-clock for these block structures: Monarch/BLAST run 1.14x-4.31x SLOWER than dense before expert kernel work; even after hand-written Triton kernels they only beat dense in the DECODE (memory-bound) regime, and there the win comes from reading FEWER WEIGHT BYTES (a quantization-like effect), not from the structure's FLOP savings — in prefill/multi-token they stay memory-bound and lose because block structure spawns b-by-n-by-r intermediates that erode the savings. Butterfly/Kronecker kernels spend up to 45-50% of runtime on memory rewriting; theoretical 1/(ad) sparsity yields only ~1.4x median speedup. This is the SAME memory-bound wall CIPHER already measured (decode MFU 0.2-23%).

HARDWARE-ACCELERATED CONTRAST: the ONLY structure where reduced FLOPs become real tokens/sec at fixed quality is 2:4 semi-structured sparsity, because Ampere+ sparse tensor cores give 2x PEAK — but realized end-to-end is only ~1.27x (vLLM + SparseGPT), pretraining-with-2:4 reaches dense-parity accuracy. Monarch/BTT/butterfly have NO such hardware peak multiplier; they are not on the tensor-core fast path.

VERDICT FOR A SUBSTRATE: Monarch/BTT/M2 are MODEL-ARCHITECTURE choices made at pretraining time. They cannot be delivered post-hoc by CIPHER on a frozen Mistral/Llama-7B (post-hoc projection is exactly what the founding showed fails on quality, and even Monarch's analytic projection needs 4000-step / GLUE fine-tuning to recover accuracy). CIPHER CAN host a checkpoint that was pretrained/finetuned WITH these layers (the way it hosts a quantized model) IF and only if someone first does the model-side training — and even then the inference win is decode-only, kernel-dependent (needs custom Triton, not cuBLAS/cutlass), and modest (~1.1-3x decode, contingent on weight-byte reduction), with the real lift being smaller model footprint rather than higher fixed-quality MFU.

methods.name: Monarch (Dao et al. 2022) — structured matrix generalizing FFT, trained-in
methods.math: Two block-diagonal factors with a permutation: M = P L P R (each L,R block-diagonal). Sub-quadratic O(n^1.5) vs dense O(n^2). Quality preserved ONLY when trained in or fine-tuned after projection — analytic projection of dense->Monarch exists but needs recovery training.
methods.measured_speedup: 2x WALL-CLOCK training speedup for ViT (ImageNet) and GPT-2 (WikiText-103) with comparable quality; GPT-2 OpenWebText pretraining 2x via 'reverse sparsification'; BERT GLUE dense->sparse fine-tune 1.7x. These are TRAINING speedups; inference wall-clock not the headline.
methods.measured_quality: 'Comparable model quality' / 'without quality drop' at GPT-2 and ViT scale when trained in. Post-hoc projection alone loses accuracy (needs fine-tune to recover) — consistent with the founding's post-hoc failure.
methods.posthoc_possible: Partially: analytic dense->Monarch projection exists, but quality requires fine-tune recovery (BERT 1.7x needed GLUE fine-tuning). Pure frozen post-hoc = the founding's failure mode. A substrate cannot deliver quality-preserving Monarch without model-side training.
methods.hardware: GPU (training benchmarks, V100/A100-era). Uses dense GEMM on block factors — NO sparse-tensor-core peak multiplier.

methods.name: Monarch Mixer (M2-BERT, Hazy Research 2023) — full architecture, attention+MLP replaced by Monarch
methods.math: Monarch matrices for both sequence-mixing (replaces attention) and dimension-mixing (replaces MLP). Sub-quadratic in seq-len AND model-dim. GEMM-based so it maps to dense matmul hardware.
methods.measured_speedup: Up to 9.1x higher throughput at sequence length 4K vs BERT; this is a LONG-SEQUENCE / attention-replacement win (sub-quadratic in n), not a per-GEMM dense-replacement win. Proof-of-concept 25.6% FLOP utilization (vs ~25% for optimized attention).
methods.measured_quality: Matches BERT-base/large on GLUE with up to 27% fewer params/FLOPs; on ImageNet beats ViT-b by 1% accuracy at half the params. Encoder/BERT-style (non-causal) — NOT a decoder 7B result.
methods.posthoc_possible: No — it is a different architecture trained from scratch. Cannot be applied to a frozen Mistral/Llama. Substrate could only host a model someone pretrained as M2.
methods.hardware: GPU, GEMM-based (deliberately hardware-friendly), but throughput win is from sub-quadratic seq-scaling not from beating dense MLP GEMMs at fixed quality.

methods.name: Block Tensor-Train BTT (Qiu/Potapczynski et al., 'Compute Better Spent' 2024) — superset of Monarch
methods.math: Block Tensor-Train: generalizes Monarch (Monarch is a special case). Full-rank no-parameter-sharing variant maximizes params-per-FLOP; N/F = Theta(d^-omega). Better scaling laws than dense for the SAME compute.
methods.measured_speedup: BTT matches dense ViT-S/32 on ImageNet-1k with 3.8x LESS COMPUTE (FLOP/train-compute, not GPU wall-clock — paper frames it as compute/scaling-law efficiency, not measured tokens/sec). 'More efficient than dense for training small GPT-2 language models' (no decoder wall-clock factor given).
methods.measured_quality: Dense-parity at iso-compute on ImageNet ViT and CIFAR MLPs/ViTs; small GPT-2 LM more efficient than dense. Strongest evidence that co-designed structure beats dense on the quality-vs-compute frontier — opposite of the frozen-model failure.
methods.posthoc_possible: No — trained from scratch; scaling-law result. Requires weight-normalization to avoid divergence. Not a frozen-weight technique.
methods.hardware: GPU/TPU training. 3.8x is COMPUTE not measured wall-clock; BTT/Monarch block structure is memory-bound on GPU at inference (see Memory-Efficient Acceleration paper) so the FLOP win does not directly become tokens/sec.

methods.name: Structured Feedforward Layers in LLMs (CLAIRE-Labo, 'Building on Efficient Foundations' NeurIPS 2024) — LowRank/BlockShuffle/BlockDense FFN, decoder, up to 1.3B
methods.math: Replace FFN dense matrices with LowRank ((M+N)R params), BlockShuffle, or BlockDense. Self-guided training (alpha-decay from dense teacher) fixes bad init dynamics. CLOSEST to CIPHER's target: decoder LLM, trained from scratch, up to 1.3B.
methods.measured_speedup: Training 1.3B at 32% FFN params: 1.35-1.36x faster training. INFERENCE: 2.5x latency speedup for LowRank at 32% params/width-5120 ONLY in compute-bound (large-batch/prefill) regime; 2.81x for BlockDense small-batch ONLY WITH a 'pre-merge' trick; otherwise decode is parallelism/memory-bound and 'may lead to WORSE latency due to doubling the number of linear projections.' Wide+structured nets: only 8-17% throughput boost on generation.
methods.measured_quality: 32% FFN params: +1.0 perplexity, cut to ~+0.4-0.5 with self-guided training. 63% params: +0.40 loss, minimal perplexity impact. Quality recoverable BUT requires training-in / self-guided schedule — not free post-hoc.
methods.posthoc_possible: No for quality — 'from initialization', self-guided training during pre-training, not post-hoc to a pretrained dense model. Decode speedup needs the pre-merge engineering trick or it regresses.
methods.hardware: GPU. Honest caveat from authors: structured FFN can move linear layers from compute-bound into MEMORY-bound, and naive structured decode is SLOWER (doubled projections). No sparse-tensor-core acceleration.

methods.name: Pixelated Butterfly (Chen/Dao et al. 2021/2022) — fixed flat-block-butterfly + low-rank sparsity, trained-in
methods.math: Fixed (data-independent) sparsity pattern = flat block butterfly + low-rank, chosen to be hardware-aligned (block-aligned for GPU). Sparsify attention+MLP. Pattern fixed before training so no mask-search overhead.
methods.measured_speedup: Up to 2.3x faster TRAINING than dense MLP-Mixer/ViT/GPT-2-small (ImageNet, WikiText-103) with no accuracy drop; 5.2x on Long-Range-Arena. 3x faster than dense (unstructured) butterfly. Training speedups, not 7B inference.
methods.measured_quality: No accuracy drop at the tested scales (ViT, MLP-Mixer, GPT-2-small) — but achieved by training with the pattern in place from the start.
methods.posthoc_possible: No — fixed sparsity pattern set before/at training; it is a sparse-training method, not a frozen-weight compression. Substrate cannot impose it post-hoc.
methods.hardware: GPU; 'hardware-aligned fixed sparsity pattern' is the explicit reason for real wall-clock gains, but still block-sparse dense-core matmul, NOT 2:4 sparse-tensor-core; gains are training-time.

methods.name: Kronecker-Sparse / Butterfly GPU inference kernels (Gonon et al. 2024) — REALITY CHECK on FLOP-vs-wallclock
methods.math: Kronecker-sparse (butterfly) factors with pattern (a,b,c,d), sparsity 1/(ad). Studies the kernel itself: memory-rewriting (transpose/reshape between factors) dominates.
methods.measured_speedup: Optimized kernel: 1.4x MEDIAN over prior butterfly bmm baselines (only ~6.57x vs dense in best memory-intensive cases; ViT modules 0.78x the time of FC). DECISIVE FINDING: existing implementations spend up to 45-50% of runtime on MEMORY REWRITING, so theoretical 1/(ad) FLOP sparsity does NOT yield proportional speedup; speedup scales with memory-op intensity not FLOP count.
methods.measured_quality: Kernel-level (inference-time), quality unchanged (exact matmul). Energy: ~0.85x (median 15% reduction).
methods.posthoc_possible: Yes for the KERNEL (exact computation of an already-Kronecker-sparse layer) — but the layer must already BE Kronecker-sparse, which requires model-side training. The kernel alone does not create the structure.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA GPU. Direct evidence that butterfly/Kronecker FLOP savings are memory-bound and under-deliver — the same wall this substrate hits.

methods.name: Memory-Efficient Acceleration of Block-Low-Rank (Monarch/BLAST) on GPU (Jan 2026) — DECISIVE wall-clock reality at 7B
methods.math: Roofline analysis of block-low-rank (BLR: Monarch, BLAST) vs dense and traditional low-rank on Llama-7B/A40. Monarch spawns b-by-n-by-r intermediates (b up to 16) -> extra data movement.
methods.measured_speedup: BEFORE kernel work: Monarch 1.14-1.68x SLOWER than dense, BLAST 2.63-4.31x SLOWER (multi-token inference). AFTER optimized Triton kernels: BLAST up to 3.76x over a PyTorch dense baseline, 3.05x end-to-end Llama-7B/A40 vs BLAST baseline; outperforms dense by 1.13-3.76x in >90% of cases — but the structural win is in SINGLE-TOKEN DECODE where 'bottleneck is weight data movement rather than compute' (i.e. a weight-byte/quantization-style win, NOT a FLOP win). In prefill/multi-token they fall BELOW the roofline breakpoint = memory-bound and underperform.
methods.measured_quality: Llama-3.2-1B compressed then FINE-TUNED 4000 steps on SlimPajama (lr 8e-4) to recover accuracy — i.e. post-hoc compression needs recovery training, echoing the founding's post-hoc-fails finding.

methods.hardware: NVIDIA A40, Jetson Orin; Llama-7B, Llama-3.2-1B, GPT2-S, ViT-B, DiT-XL/2. Confirms: structured-matrix FLOP reduction != tokens/sec on GPU; only memory-bound decode benefits, via fewer weight bytes.

methods.name: 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparsity (HARDWARE-ACCELERATED CONTRAST — the only structure on the tensor-core fast path)
methods.math: Exactly 2 of every 4 weights nonzero. Ampere+ sparse tensor cores give 2x PEAK throughput for 2:4. This is the ONE structured pattern with a real hardware peak multiplier (unlike Monarch/BTT/butterfly).
methods.measured_speedup: Tensor-core 2:4 = up to 2x peak; realized end-to-end LLM inference ~1.27x (SparseGPT post-training prune + vLLM). Pre-training WITH 2:4 reaches dense-parity accuracy; activation-2:4 work (2025) targets train+inference.
methods.measured_quality: Transformers pre-trained with 2:4 are 'comparable or even superior' to dense; post-training 2:4 (SparseGPT) near-lossless on many LLMs. Quality best when co-designed at pretraining.
methods.posthoc_possible: Yes — post-training SparseGPT 2:4 prune is genuinely post-hoc and vLLM-servable (~1.27x), making it the most substrate-deliverable structured option, BUT the 2x is a hardware-peak effect, realized only ~1.27x end-to-end, and is sparsity not the Monarch/BTT structured-matrix family. Included as the honest 'what actually raises tokens/sec' contrast.
methods.hardware: NVIDIA Ampere/Hopper sparse tensor cores; served via vLLM. The only family where reduced effective FLOPs map to a real (capped, ~1.27x) tokens/sec gain at fixed quality.

assessment.method: Kronecker-Sparse / Butterfly GPU inference kernels (Gonon et al. 2024/2025, "Fast Inference with Kronecker-Sparse Matrices", arXiv:2405.15013, ICML 2025). Fused output-stationary CUDA/OpenCL kernel for Kronecker-sparse (butterfly/Monarch) factors with pattern (a,b,c,d), sparsity 1/(ad); headline contribution is eliminating the memory-rewriting (transpose/reshape) that dominates prior butterfly bmm kernels. Repo: github.com/PascalCarrivain/ksmm (KSLinear drop-in).
assessment.honest_gain: For CIPHER's target (H100, FP16/BF16, 7B-dense, preserved quality): expect roughly NO net tokens/sec gain, plausibly a regression. Decisive numbers: (1) The kernel's x1.4 median is FP32 and is vs OTHER butterfly kernels (bmm/einsum/bsr), NOT vs dense cuBLAS. (2) In half-precision (the regime H100 LLM serving uses) the kernel beats those butterfly baselines on only 37.8% of patterns, down from 85% in FP32; authors explicitly state existing baselines 'benefit more from tensor cores' and the KS kernel does not. The win mechanism (eliminating memory rewriting) erodes once FP16 tensor cores are in play. (3) Best real end-to-end MODEL result: GPT-2 Medium x1.19 (16% latency cut) in FP32 on an RTX6000, by KS-factoring a SINGLE 1024x4096 FFN down-proj at 24.8% sparsity; ViT-S/16 x1.28 FP32 on A100. ZERO H100 measurements, ZERO 7B-LLM, and the end-to-end gains are FP32 (the precision where the kernel is strongest). (4) KS/butterfly reduces FLOPs but is NOT a hardware-accelerated primitive like 2:4 sparse tensor cores (which alone give the real 2x peak). At 7B decode, serving is memory-bandwidth-bound (weight movement); corroborating commentary notes block-low-rank/Monarch 'achieve similar performance to dense since the bottleneck is weight data movement.' Honest expected H100/7B/FP16/quality-preserved throughput gain: ~1.0x (noise); upside maybe ~1.1x ONLY in a compute-bound prefill/large-batch corner on specific shapes, with real downside risk of slowdown because the kernel is unoptimized for FP16 tensor cores.
assessment.delivery: CIPHER would HOST a co-designed checkpoint, not invent one, and that part is genuinely feasible: the repo ships a PyTorch KSLinear drop-in, structurally analogous to hosting a quantized checkpoint (swap dense Linear for a KS-factored module + custom kernel under unmodified vLLM). BUT two delivery problems are fatal for the stated goal. (a) QUALITY requires real model-side work: the paper measures latency only and NEVER measures accuracy; it picks patterns with >=0.75 of dense param-count only 'to raise hope it could yield competitive accuracy IF fine-tuned or trained from scratch' (Dao/Monarch co-design protocol). Preserved quality is unproven and demands prune+calibration or light finetune; this is not a frozen-model lever, consistent with the founding's post-hoc Monarch/Kronecker failure. (b) The custom kernel is the asset and it is tuned for ONE ViT batch (25,088) / ~700 patterns on A100/RTX6000 in FP32; there is no H100 build, no FP16 tensor-core optimization, so CIPHER would have to write/tune a new H100 FP16/BF16 KS kernel that, per the paper's own FP16 data, is unlikely to beat cuBLAS dense.
assessment.reasoning: Verified skeptically against the full paper PDF (28pp, arXiv:2405.15013, extracted locally), the v2 HTML, and the ksmm repo README. (1) Speedup REAL on H100? No H100 anywhere (A100 + RTX6000 only; 0 H100 hits in the PDF). The x1.4 is FP32-and-vs-butterfly-baselines, not vs dense; in FP16 the win-rate collapses to 37.8% of patterns by the authors' own Table 9, attributed to baselines exploiting tensor cores, exactly the FLOP-reduction-does-not-raise-throughput trap. The headline >x6 'vs dense' holds only because KS patterns are extremely sparse (1/(ad)), an apples-to-oranges FLOP comparison, not a fixed-quality throughput win. (2) Quality honest? The paper measures NO accuracy; quality preservation is hope-conditional-on-finetune/train-from-scratch, i.e. co-design, not post-hoc, matching the 'no-pure-posthoc' tag and the founding's documented post-hoc Monarch failure. (3) What CIPHER ships: hosting a co-designed checkpoint is feasible (quant-like; KSLinear exists), but inventing the quality-preserving model is the infeasible part (needs retraining the structure in), and the kernel asset does not exist for H100 FP16. (4) Honest gain ~1.0x at the target operating point; the only real measured model-level gains (x1.19 to x1.28) are FP32, tiny-model, single-layer, non-H100, quality untested. Cross-check: independent commentary confirms block-low-rank/Monarch achieve similar performance to dense in bandwidth-bound single-token decode. Bottom line: a clean academic kernel-engineering result (real 1.4x over PRIOR butterfly kernels in FP32) that does NOT translate to a quality-preserving tokens/sec win for H100/7B-dense FP16 serving; it is FLOP reduction that does not survive contact with FP16 tensor cores. Uncertainty caveat: I could not access OpenReview reviewer threads (fetch returned only the abstract) and there is no independent H100 reproduction of KS LLM serving, so the 'plausible FP16 slowdown' is inferred from the authors' own FP16 ablation, not a separately measured H100 number. Key sources: arxiv.org/abs/2405.15013, arxiv.org/html/2405.15013v2, github.com/PascalCarrivain/ksmm.
