assessment.method: Memory-Efficient Acceleration of Block-Low-Rank (Monarch/BLAST) on GPU — block-low-rank weight factorization (Monarch, BLAST) with custom Triton kernels. Source papers: BLAST (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2410.21262) and the Jan-2026 acceleration paper (arXiv 2512.20861, code github.com/pabillam/mem-efficient-blr).
assessment.honest_gain: For H100 / 7B-dense / preserved-quality: essentially ZERO usable throughput gain, and quality is NOT preserved. Honest expectation: (a) Speedup is real ONLY on resource-constrained GPUs (A40 40GB, Jetson Orin Nano 8GB) at batch=1 single-token decode, where it is a weight-byte-movement win (quantization-style, ~2x compression), NOT a FLOP/MFU win — the paper explicitly states the bottleneck is 'weight data movement rather than compute.' (b) On compute-bound multi-token/prefill, the UNoptimized kernels are 1.14-1.68x SLOWER (Monarch) / 2.63-4.31x SLOWER (BLAST) than dense; the headline 3.05-3.76x 'speedups' are vs a PyTorch DENSE baseline on a memory-constrained GPU, and the structural intermediates (b-by-n-by-r, b up to 16) ADD data movement. (c) No H100 results exist; H100 has 3.35 TB/s HBM and fast tensor cores, so the memory-bound single-token win that powers this method largely evaporates there. (d) Quality is a hard fail: even AFTER fine-tuning, BLAST 50%-compressed Llama-3.2-1B = WikiText-2 ppl 20.10 vs dense 11.57 (+74%) and zero-shot 46.37% vs 56.54% (-10.2 pts). Original BLAST Llama-7B needed retraining on 0.49B tokens (400 steps) to reach 'lowest degradation' — still degraded. Without retraining: 'at most 4x higher perplexity and 25% accuracy degradation.'
assessment.delivery: CIPHER could HOST a BLAST/Monarch-factorized checkpoint the same way it hosts a quantized one — the structured GEMM is a substrate-legal kernel swap (custom Triton/cutlass kernel intercepting the linear layers). That part is feasible. BUT CIPHER cannot INVENT the checkpoint: the method's entire value depends on co-design = prune-to-block-structure PLUS recovery fine-tuning (400-4000 steps on SlimPajama, lr 8e-4, 0.49B tokens), which is model-side training work CIPHER explicitly does not do. So delivery = host-a-co-designed-checkpoint is mechanically feasible, but it would ship the quality regression baked into that checkpoint (+74% ppl / -10pt accuracy at 50% compression), and on H100 it would NOT deliver a throughput gain because the win is memory-bound single-token on small GPUs, not compute-bound batched serving on H100. Net: not shippable as a quality-preserving speedup.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification against the four required tests. (1) SPEEDUP REAL ON H100? NO. All measurements are on A40 and Jetson Orin Nano at batch=1; the paper title literally says 'Resource Constrained GPUs.' The win mechanism is reduced weight-byte movement in single-token decode (memory-bound) — the paper's own roofline puts Monarch/BLAST BELOW the breakpoint (memory-bound) while dense and traditional low-rank are compute-bound (above breakpoint). On compute-bound multi-token they UNDERPERFORM dense (1.14-4.31x slower pre-kernel). H100's high HBM bandwidth + tensor cores shrinks exactly the regime where this helps. This is NOT a 2:4-sparse-tensor-core hardware-accelerated structure that raises peak; block-low-rank lowers the FLOP numerator and adds intermediate data movement — the textbook FLOP-reduction-not-throughput trap, made worse by extra intermediates. The '3.76x' is the post-Triton-kernel number recovering from a self-inflicted 4.31x slowdown, measured against a dense PyTorch baseline on a small GPU. (2) QUALITY HONEST? The papers are honest that it needs recovery fine-tuning and still degrades. The numbers are damning at 7B-relevant scale: BLAST-50% leaves a +74% perplexity gap and -10pt zero-shot AFTER 4000 steps of fine-tuning; Monarch fails to recover at 50% ('Monarch and Block-Diagonal fail to recover acceptable performance'). This directly echoes the CIPHER founding's post-hoc-low-rank failure (full-layer rank-k -> KL=13 mode collapse): co-design with light finetune does NOT close the quality gap to dense at the 2x compression needed for a speedup. (3) WHAT CIPHER SHIPS: hosting a co-designed checkpoint is feasible (kernel swap, like quant); inventing it is infeasible (requires training). But hosting it imports the quality regression and yields no H100 throughput win. (4) HONEST GAIN: ~0 quality-preserving throughput on H100/7B-dense. Cross-corroborated by two independent papers + roofline analysis + the memory-bound-decode literature confirming structured methods give only 1.07-1.21x in memory-bound decode and that decode tok/s scales with HBM bandwidth not FLOPs. CONCLUSION: quality-killer (primary) with strong flop-reduction-not-throughput characteristics. The verdict 'quality-killer' is chosen because the dominant, decisive failure for a quality-preserving mandate is the +74% perplexity / -10pt accuracy at the 2x compression required to get any speed — and even setting quality aside, the speed is memory-bound-small-GPU-only, not H100 throughput.

method.name: 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparsity (HARDWARE-ACCELERATED CONTRAST — the only structure on the tensor-core fast path)
method.math: Exactly 2 of every 4 weights nonzero. Ampere+ sparse tensor cores give 2x PEAK throughput for 2:4. This is the ONE structured pattern with a real hardware peak multiplier (unlike Monarch/BTT/butterfly).
method.measured_speedup: Tensor-core 2:4 = up to 2x peak; realized end-to-end LLM inference ~1.27x (SparseGPT post-training prune + vLLM). Pre-training WITH 2:4 reaches dense-parity accuracy; activation-2:4 work (2025) targets train+inference.
method.measured_quality: Transformers pre-trained with 2:4 are 'comparable or even superior' to dense; post-training 2:4 (SparseGPT) near-lossless on many LLMs. Quality best when co-designed at pretraining.
method.posthoc_possible: Yes — post-training SparseGPT 2:4 prune is genuinely post-hoc and vLLM-servable (~1.27x), making it the most substrate-deliverable structured option, BUT the 2x is a hardware-peak effect, realized only ~1.27x end-to-end, and is sparsity not the Monarch/BTT structured-matrix family. Included as the honest 'what actually raises tokens/sec' contrast.
method.hardware: NVIDIA Ampere/Hopper sparse tensor cores; served via vLLM. The only family where reduced effective FLOPs map to a real (capped, ~1.27x) tokens/sec gain at fixed quality.

assessment.method: 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparsity (Ampere+ sparse tensor cores, exactly 2 of every 4 weights nonzero; the only structured pattern with a real hardware peak multiplier)
assessment.honest_gain: Honest H100 / 7B-dense / preserved-quality gain: ~1.1-1.3x, and ONLY in compute-bound regimes (prefill, or decode batch >16). Kernel-level reality on H100 (cuSPARSELt, NVIDIA's own numbers): 2:4 FP8 GEMM hits 1900 TFLOPS vs dense 1500 TFLOPS = 1.27x, NOT the 2x peak — because the sparse kernel realizes only 47.5% of its theoretical peak while dense realizes 75%. End-to-end LLM: the rigorous Red Hat/vLLM benchmark isolates SPARSITY-ALONE at just 1.1-1.2x; the widely-cited "1.27x" (hpc-ai, Llama-3-8B, 123.66s->97.64s) is sparse+FP8 COMBINED, and Neural Magic's "1.7x on GPU" is best-case. In the regime CIPHER actually lives in — 7B-dense batch=1 decode, memory-bound (per CIPHER memory: 0.2-23% MFU) — the tensor-core 2x is NOT realized at all (CUTLASS 2:4 only beats dense at batch >16); the only decode benefit is a ~28-37% weight-byte reduction from the compressed format (metadata overhead prevents a clean 50%), giving a modest HBM-bandwidth win, not 2x throughput.
assessment.delivery: CIPHER ships this by HOSTING a co-designed checkpoint (feasible, exactly like it hosts a quantized one) — it CANNOT invent it. The "light-calibration-only" framing in the brief is FALSE per the evidence: one-shot SparseGPT 2:4 (the calibration-only path) collapses quality — Sparse Llama Table 1: 77.1% eval recovery at 50% sparsity / 34.5% at 70%; hpc-ai MMLU 0.667->0.404 (5-shot, no finetune). Reaching dense-parity requires SPARSE PRETRAINING: 45B tokens (50%) to 100B tokens (70%) of retraining (~2-8% of Llama-2's 2T), e.g. 13B-token curated runs taking 26h on 32xH100, plus SquareHead layerwise distillation, to land at 96.1% (50%) / 91.8% (70%) recovery — still slightly below dense. The "comparable or even superior" pretraining-with-2:4 claim is BERT/GLUE (79.6 vs 79.8 dense), NOT a validated dense-parity result for 7B+ generative LLMs without massive compute. So: CIPHER consumes an off-the-shelf co-designed checkpoint (RedHatAI/Neural-Magic Sparse-Llama-2of4, optionally +W4A16) and serves it via its cuBLAS/cutlass GEMM interposition swapped to a cuSPARSELt 2:4 path — feasible and substrate-legal. It cannot produce the checkpoint (pretraining-scale work is out of substrate scope). Net deployable: ~1.1-1.3x prefill/large-batch throughput at near-dense quality IF a co-designed checkpoint exists; ~1.0x for single-stream 7B decode.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification against the four required gates. (1) REAL on H100, not paper-FLOP? Partially real but heavily overstated: the 2x is PEAK only; cuSPARSELt realizes 1.27x at the GEMM level (1900 vs 1500 TFLOPS, NVIDIA's own measurement) and ~1.1-1.2x end-to-end from sparsity alone. Crucially, the speedup is conditional on COMPUTE-bound execution (batch >16); the founding correctly noted 7B decode is memory-bound at 0.2-23% MFU, where 2:4 weight sparsity yields no tensor-core throughput gain, only a partial weight-byte/bandwidth reduction. This is the SAME compute-bound-only trap the founding hit with W4A16 (fired only at M=1, opposite corner) — neither corner gives a clean win at fixed quality. So it is NOT pure flop-reduction (the hardware multiplier is genuine on the fast path), which is why I did NOT pick 'flop-reduction-not-throughput'; but it is materially overstated relative to '2x' and the conditions are narrow. (2) Quality cost honest? The brief's 'light-calibration-only' is contradicted by every rigorous source: post-hoc/one-shot 2:4 is a quality killer (34.5-77.1% recovery; MMLU -39% relative), and only pretraining-scale retraining (45B-100B tokens) restores near-parity. This is the founding's exact lesson (structure imposed post-hoc on a frozen model fails) reconfirmed for the one hardware-accelerated pattern. (3) What CIPHER ships: host a co-designed checkpoint = feasible (like quant); invent it = infeasible (needs pretraining compute, out of substrate scope). (4) The honest answer to the KEY QUESTION: co-design DOES recover quality, but it requires pretraining-scale work, not light calibration — so 2:4 is genuinely the best of the structured levers (real hardware peak), yet the quality-preserving version is gated behind heavy model-side retraining and the realized inference gain at fixed quality is a modest ~1.1-1.3x in compute-bound regimes only. Verdict 'real-but-needs-finetune' captures both that the hardware acceleration is real (unlike Monarch/Koopman/butterfly) AND that quality preservation is impossible with the claimed light calibration. I considered 'real-2x-hardware' (rejected: 2x is peak-only, 1.27x realized, and absent in decode) and 'overstated' (the gain is real and substrate-shippable on the right checkpoint+regime, so not merely overstated). Sources: NVIDIA cuSPARSELt/Ampere sparsity blog + CUDALibrarySamples (kernel 1.27x, 47.5% of peak); Red Hat 2:4 Sparse Llama article (sparsity-alone 1.1-1.2x, MMLU table); hpc-ai 1.27x blog (sparse+FP8, MMLU 0.667->0.404->0.604); Cerebras/Neural-Magic Sparse Llama arXiv:2405.03594 (Table 1: 77.1%/34.5% one-shot vs 96.1%/91.8% with 45B/100B-token sparse pretraining, 1.7x nm-vllm); CUTLASS batch>16 constraint and decode memory-bound critiques; arXiv:2404.01847 pretraining-with-2:4 (BERT GLUE 79.6 vs 79.8, not a 7B LLM dense-parity proof).

research.summary: VERDICT FOR CIPHER: Unlike the founding's post-hoc weight-factorization failures, the attention/KV-cache area has a clear class of CO-DESIGNED wins that preserve quality with LIGHT finetune (single-digit-billions of tokens) or pure post-hoc calibration, and several of them are RETROFITTABLE to a trained checkpoint the way CIPHER hosts a quantized model. The single most important nuance for CIPHER's FLOP-vs-MFU worry: the winning attention math does NOT reduce FLOPs. MLA/latent attention INCREASES attention FLOPs (~4x vs MHA, ~22x vs GQA per General Compute's analysis) but raises arithmetic intensity by roughly 200x, moving long-context DECODE attention off the memory-bandwidth wall and toward compute-bound on H100 (~1 FLOP/byte -> approaching the ~295 FLOP/byte roofline). That is the right kind of lever: it raises real decode tokens/sec at long context by using the hardware better, not by lowering the numerator. This is the opposite failure mode from naive low-rank-on-weights (which lowers FLOPs but stays memory-bound and loses quality). The two regimes matter: (A) Long-context / large-batch decode is KV-cache-dominated and memory-bound -> here KV compression (MLA, KV low-rank, KV quantization) gives REAL measured wall-clock speedups (1.9x-10x+) at preserved quality. (B) Short-context decode is launch/weight-bound -> KV methods give little. CIPHER targets H100 7B-dense; the biggest realistic wins are at long context. THREE actionable families: (1) MLA-via-TransMLA retrofit of GQA Llama/Mistral: NeurIPS-2025 spotlight, 93% KV compression on Llama-2-7B, claimed ~10x decode speedup at 8K, needs ~6B-token light finetune; production-validated (Ant Ling-2.5-1T). This answers the explicit question: YES, MLA is retrofittable to a trained GQA model, but it requires finetune, not pure post-hoc. (2) KV quantization: KIVI/KVQuant are essentially post-hoc (no finetune); BitDecoding (2025) is the standout because it uses TENSOR CORES for low-bit KV attention -> 7.5x (4090) / 8x (H100) kernel speedup vs FP16 FlashDecoding and 3x end-to-end decode-latency cut on Llama-3.1-8B at 128K, with only 0.2% (4-bit) accuracy loss, post-hoc. This is the closest analog to the 2:4-sparse-tensor-core 'real MFU' lever the prompt flags. (3) Palu KV low-rank: post-hoc decomposition + light calibration, 1.89x attention speedup at 50% compression (2.91x with quant). Linear/SSM hybrids (Mamba-in-Llama) work but need 20B-token distillation and lose general-benchmark quality (MMLU -10pts at 50% attn-replacement) -> too much model-side work and quality risk for a 7B-dense drop-in. HONESTY FLAGS: TransMLA's 10.6x is a KV-memory/batch-capacity-driven serving number at 8K, not a pure per-token kernel speedup, and the founding-style caution applies; the quality 'on par' is benchmark-level, not loss-level. GLA (Hardware-Efficient Attention, 2025) needs training from scratch -> NOT retrofittable, excluded as a drop-in.

methods.name: TransMLA: GQA-to-MLA retrofit (light finetune)
methods.math: Re-expresses trained GQA KV projections as Multi-head Latent Attention: replaces per-head K/V with a shared low-rank latent c (DeepSeek-V2 MLA), with two execution paths (MHA-expand for prefill, MQA-absorb for decode). GQA is provably a special case of MLA at equal KV size, so the conversion is exact-at-init, then light finetune restores the extra MLA expressivity. Note: MLA increases attention FLOPs but raises arithmetic intensity ~200x, so decode moves from memory-bound toward compute-bound.
methods.measured_speedup: Claimed ~10.6x inference speedup at 8K context on Llama-2-7B (driven by 93% KV-cache compression enabling far larger batch / less HBM traffic). This is a serving/throughput number, NOT a pure per-token kernel speedup; no isolated wall-clock decode-kernel factor is reported in the paper.
methods.measured_quality: Performance 'on par with original across multiple benchmarks' after finetune. Concrete point: Qwen2.5-7B GSM8K 82.11% (TransMLA) vs 81.96% (GQA baseline). Quality stated at benchmark level, not at loss/PPL level; some versions report no perplexity. Quality recovery REQUIRES the finetune.
methods.posthoc_possible: Partial: the algebraic GQA->MLA conversion is post-hoc and exact-at-init, but recovering/exceeding original quality requires ~6B tokens of finetuning. Cannot be deployed as pure zero-touch post-hoc. CIPHER could HOST the converted MLA checkpoint (DeepSeek-compatible, runs under vLLM/SGLang) the way it hosts a quantized model.
methods.hardware: GPU (vLLM/SGLang via DeepSeek MLA kernels). Production-adopted in Ant Group Ling-2.5-1T. NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight.

methods.name: BitDecoding: tensor-core low-bit KV-cache attention
methods.math: Quantizes KV cache to 4-bit/2-bit (incl. native MXFP4 on Blackwell) and, crucially, runs the low-bit KV attention on TENSOR CORES cooperatively with CUDA cores (not just dequant-then-fp16). Dynamic online quantization during autoregressive decode. This is the hardware-accelerated-structure lever analogous to 2:4 sparse tensor cores: it raises achieved throughput, not just lowers memory.
methods.measured_speedup: Attention-kernel: up to 7.5x (RTX 4090), 8.0x (H100), 4.8x (A100) vs FP16 FlashDecoding-v2; up to 4.3x vs QServe. End-to-end: 3x single-batch decode-latency reduction on Llama-3.1-8B at 128K context; >4x serving throughput vs QServe. Real wall-clock.
methods.measured_quality: 4-bit KV: 0.2% accuracy degradation on LongBench. 2-bit KV: 2.7% degradation (with 4.25x throughput vs FP16). Strong at 4-bit, acceptable-with-loss at 2-bit.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES, fully post-hoc. Uses dynamic online quantization during decode with no offline calibration and no retrain. This is the most directly CIPHER-aligned: a kernel/substrate-level swap on a frozen model that yields real long-context decode speedup via tensor cores.
methods.hardware: H100 (Hopper), RTX 4090 (Ada), A100 (Ampere), RTX 5090 / Blackwell (MXFP4). Long-context (128K) is where it pays off.

methods.name: KVQuant: per-channel pre-RoPE non-uniform KV quantization
methods.math: 3-bit (and lower) KV quantization with: per-channel Key quantization (matches Key outlier-along-channel distribution), pre-RoPE Key quantization, per-layer sensitivity-weighted non-uniform datatypes (nuq), and per-vector dense-and-sparse outlier isolation. Reduces KV HBM footprint to break the memory-bandwidth wall in long-context decode.
methods.measured_speedup: ~4.8x reduction in KV activation memory at 3-bit; enables Llama-7B at 1M context on a single A100-80GB (10M on 8 GPUs). Memory/capacity-driven throughput; the paper's headline is footprint and context-length, not a single decode-kernel speedup factor (vs BitDecoding which provides tensor-core kernel speedups).
methods.measured_quality: <0.1 perplexity degradation at 3-bit on Wikitext-2 and C4 (Llama / Llama-2 / Llama-3 / Mistral). Near-lossless at 3-bit.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES, post-hoc. Needs a one-time offline calibration to fit the non-uniform datatypes and outlier sets; no gradient finetune, no weight change. NeurIPS 2024.
methods.hardware: A100-80GB (single and 8-GPU); applies to GPU long-context serving.

methods.name: KIVI: tuning-free asymmetric 2-bit KV quantization
methods.math: Asymmetric scheme: quantize Key cache per-channel, Value cache per-token (matches their differing outlier structure), with streaming/grouped quantization and fused dequant+matmul kernels.
methods.measured_speedup: Up to 3.47x throughput improvement and up to 2.6x peak-memory reduction (incl. weights). Throughput gain is largest at large batch / long context where KV dominates.
methods.measured_quality: 'Little to no accuracy drop' at 2-bit on Llama-2, Falcon, Mistral across benchmarks. (Newer work, e.g. Kitty 2025, notes 2-bit can hurt some long-128K tasks and adds dynamic channel-wise precision boost to recover.)
methods.posthoc_possible: YES, fully tuning-free and plug-and-play. No calibration, no finetune, no weight change. ICML 2024. Directly hostable by a CIPHER-style substrate.
methods.hardware: GPU (fused CUDA kernels); Llama/Falcon/Mistral 7B-class.

methods.name: Palu: low-rank KV-cache projection (+ optional quant)
methods.math: Compresses the KV hidden dimension via medium-grained low-rank SVD-style decomposition of the K/V projections, with a rank-search algorithm, low-rank-aware quantization, and a fused GPU kernel. Reduces KV bytes read per decode step. Note: this IS a low-rank-on-attention approach but applied to KV projections (not the dense MLP weights the founding tried), and combined with calibration so it works where the founding's full-layer rank-k collapsed.
methods.measured_speedup: Up to 1.89x speedup on the RoPE-based attention module at 50% KV compression; up to 2.91x when combined with quantization (over 91.25% / 11.4x total compression). Real fused-kernel wall-clock.
methods.measured_quality: Maintains strong zero-shot accuracy and perplexity at 50% compression; reports up to 1.19 lower perplexity than quantization-only baselines at matched compression.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES, post-training. Decomposition + calibration-based rank search on a frozen model; no gradient finetune. ICLR 2025. Contrast with founding's failed full-layer rank-k: Palu succeeds because it targets KV projections at moderate rank with calibration, not aggressive whole-weight factorization.
methods.hardware: GPU (custom fused kernel with matrix fusion); RoPE-based 7B LLMs.

methods.name: Mamba-in-Llama: Transformer->hybrid-SSM distillation
methods.math: Replaces a fraction of attention layers with Mamba SSM layers initialized FROM the attention weights (linear-attention view), then multistage distillation (KL pseudo-label + SFT + DPO). SSM decode is O(1)-state per step (no growing KV), so long-context decode is not KV-memory-bound at all.
methods.measured_speedup: ~1.8x generation speedup (Mamba-Zephyr hybrid, RTX 3090) and ~1.85-2x for pure Mamba 7B/2.8B (H100, 272/421 tok/s) with hardware-aware speculative decoding; pure Mamba cited at up to 5x throughput vs Transformer. Largest gains at long context / large batch.
methods.measured_quality: At 50% attention retention: matches teacher on chat (AlpacaEval-2 LC 29.61% vs Llama-3-8B 22.9%) and on a 10-task LM-Eval average (64.38 vs 64.48). BUT MMLU drops ~10pts (57.81% vs 68.12%). Replacing more attention (25%/12.5%) degrades general benchmarks further.
methods.posthoc_possible: NO. Requires ~20B tokens of multistage distillation (init-from-attention helps but is not enough). Architecture change is large and general-knowledge quality regresses; high model-side cost and quality risk for a 7B-dense drop-in. Listed for completeness, not recommended as a near-term CIPHER lever.
methods.hardware: H100 / RTX 3090; Zephyr-7B, Llama-3-8B-Instruct.

methods.name: MLA arithmetic-intensity mechanism (why it raises real throughput) + GLA contrast
methods.math: MLA/latent attention loads ONE shared latent head and reuses it for both K and V states, increasing arithmetic intensity rather than cutting FLOPs. General Compute analysis: MLA ~4x FLOPs vs MHA, ~22x vs GQA, but ~200x higher arithmetic intensity, flipping decode attention from memory-bound (~1 FLOP/byte) toward H100's ~295 FLOP/byte compute roofline. Grouped Latent Attention (GLA) shards the latent head for TP. This is the load-bearing explanation for the FLOP-vs-MFU question: the win comes from intensity/hardware-fit, not numerator reduction.
methods.measured_speedup: GLA vs FlashMLA: ~20% faster at decode (qlen=1), >2x faster with speculative decoding (qlen>=2); up to 2x (and 2.7x under imbalanced sequence lengths) higher end-to-end throughput vs MLA on DeepSeek-Coder-V2, 8xH100. Confirms latent attention is genuinely faster at decode, not just smaller.
methods.measured_quality: GLA-2 at 1.47B scale: perplexity 10.218 vs MLA 10.256; downstream 60.0% vs MLA 59.1% (quality preserved/slightly better at equal KV).
methods.posthoc_possible: NO for GLA specifically (trained from scratch, NOT retrofittable). Included as the mechanistic evidence that the MLA family's speedup is real arithmetic-intensity gain on H100 (relevant to whether reducing FLOPs vs raising intensity is the right lever). For a retrofittable path use TransMLA above.
methods.hardware: 8xH100; DeepSeek-Coder-V2; 1.47B ablation models.

assessment.method: TransMLA: GQA-to-MLA retrofit (light finetune) — re-expresses trained GQA K/V projections as DeepSeek-V2 Multi-head Latent Attention (shared low-rank latent c), exact-at-init (GQA is a special case of MLA at equal KV size), then a light finetune restores MLA expressivity. Two execution paths: MHA-expand for prefill, MQA-absorb for decode. NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight (arXiv 2502.07864).
assessment.honest_gain: For CIPHER's target (single H100, 7B-dense, quality preserved): realistically ~1.5-3x DECODE/SERVING THROUGHPUT at long context (>=8K) and high concurrency, NOT 10.6x, and NOT a per-token kernel speedup. The paper's own data shows the speedup is hardware-dependent and collapses on bigger/faster GPUs: 10.6x is on a 24GB/165 TFLOPS consumer GPU at 8K; on the 40GB/312 TFLOPS and 64GB/320 TFLOPS datacenter-class platforms the paper reports only roughly 2-3x at 8K (the v5 page estimates higher ~6-8x but the unambiguous trend is monotonic decline with more memory/compute). H100 (80GB, ~990 TFLOPS BF16) sits further along that curve, so expect the LOW end. The mechanism is 93% KV-cache compression -> less HBM traffic + larger batch -> a MEMORY-BOUND throughput win, NOT a tensor-core-peak win. At short context / low concurrency / batch=1 the gain is small-to-nil because there is no KV-cache memory pressure to relieve. Quality is preserved ONLY at modest compression training-free (68.75% compression = 1.65% avg drop) OR after a 6B-token (LLaMA-2-7B; 500M-1B for smaller) finetune that fully recovers baseline at 93% compression (43.26% -> 58.68% avg). Net honest expected gain at preserved quality: a real but modest throughput multiplier in long-context/high-batch regimes, requiring model-side conversion + finetune that CIPHER does not perform.
assessment.delivery: host-a-co-designed-checkpoint (feasible, like quant — NOT invent). TransMLA is an architecture-MIGRATION tool: it emits a converted, DeepSeek-MLA-compatible checkpoint that runs under vLLM/SGLang. That output is a standard hostable checkpoint, exactly the class of artifact CIPHER already hosts (it hosts a quantized checkpoint the same way). CIPHER does NOT and cannot do the model-side work itself: the conversion + LoRA/full finetune (500M-6B tokens, ~hours on 8 GPUs) is offline retraining outside CIPHER's driver-interposition scope. So CIPHER's role is: ship/serve a third-party-or-customer-converted-and-finetuned MLA checkpoint, not produce one. Caveat for multi-GPU serving: MLA replicates the latent KV on every tensor-parallel rank (non-scaling decode term), so the memory win partly evaporates under TP and needs data-parallel attention (DP+EP) to realize at high concurrency — a deployment constraint, not a blocker for single-H100 7B.
assessment.reasoning: VERIFIED numbers from arXiv 2502.07864 (v4/v5) and the NeurIPS poster. ADVERSARIAL VERDICT on the four skeptic questions: (1) Is the speedup REAL on H100, not paper-FLOP? Partly. It is real throughput, NOT a FLOP-accounting trick — MLA genuinely RAISES arithmetic intensity (~200x via decode absorb, moving decode toward compute-bound, the opposite of FLOP-reduction lowering the numerator). BUT it is also NOT a hardware-peak win like 2:4 sparse tensor cores; it is a KV-cache-memory/HBM-bandwidth/batch win. The headline 10.6x is on a memory-starved 24GB consumer GPU; the paper's own figures show it shrinks to ~2-3x (v4 read) on 40-64GB datacenter GPUs, and H100 would be lower still. No isolated decode-kernel wall-clock factor is reported anywhere — the gain is a serving/throughput aggregate. So on H100/7B the realistic win is modest and regime-gated (long context + high batch). (2) Is the quality cost honest? YES, and it is finetune-gated and disclosed: training-free is only safe at 68.75% compression (1.65% drop); at the 93% compression that drives the 10.6x claim, training-free costs a catastrophic 27.78% avg accuracy drop, recovered ONLY by a 6B-token finetune. The GSM8K 82.11 vs 81.96 (Qwen2.5-7B) point in the prompt is real but is the dimensionality-expansion ABLATION, not the headline conversion result. So 'on par with original' is true STRICTLY post-finetune. (3) What would CIPHER ship? Host a converted checkpoint (feasible) — it cannot invent/finetune one. (4) This is fundamentally different from the FOUNDING failures: those imposed structure POST-HOC on a frozen model and broke (Koopman KL=13, Monarch 23/32 full-rank). TransMLA succeeds precisely because it CO-DESIGNS via finetune — confirming the user's thesis that the structure must be earned with calibration/finetune, not stamped on a frozen model. Net: a legitimate co-design result, honestly reported, but the H100/7B/preserved-quality gain is far below the 10.6x banner and is throughput-at-long-context, not a per-token or tensor-core-peak speedup. Cross-checked against MLA-TP replication limitation (multiple 2025-2026 sources) and the MHA2MLA comparison. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2502.07864 (v4 html, v5 pdf), neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/117839, openreview.net/forum?id=TcVCu2PKb9, arxiv.org/pdf/2508.15881 (TPLA on MLA-TP replication), github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/15162.

assessment.method: BitDecoding (HPCA 2026, arXiv:2503.18773) — tensor-core low-bit KV-cache decode attention. Quantizes the KV cache to 4-bit/2-bit ONLINE during autoregressive decode and runs the low-bit KV attention COOPERATIVELY on tensor cores + CUDA cores via a "BitFusion" layout, instead of the naive dequant-then-FP16 path. Keeps a small FP16 residual buffer of recent tokens (<256, <1% of a 32K+ cache) and uses tensor-wise OR channel-wise scaling. No weight changes, no finetune, no calibration.
assessment.honest_gain: Real wall-clock on H100, but the 8.9x headline is KERNEL-ONLY and BATCHED. From the paper: H100 attention kernel 4-bit = 3.5x single-query / 9.0x batched vs FP16 FlashDecoding-v3; 2-bit higher. End-to-end is far lower and CONTEXT-GATED: ~3x single-batch decode-latency reduction on Llama-3.1-8B ONLY at 128K context; serving throughput INT4 ~2.98x / INT2 ~4.25x at 32K (Table I). At short/medium context (CIPHER's typical 7B-dense regime) the gain is ~0 because decode attention is not yet KV-bandwidth-bound — speedup grows with context length and batch. This is genuine hardware-accelerated structure (cuts KV memory traffic AND uses tensor cores), not FLOP-reduction-that-lowers-the-numerator; corroborated by vLLM's FP8-KV measurements (~1.5-2x throughput from KV-byte halving alone). Honest H100/7B-dense/preserved-quality expectation: 4-bit at LONG context (>=32K, batched) ~2-3x end-to-end decode throughput at ~-0.2% LongBench (near-lossless, post-hoc, no finetune); near-zero at short context. 2-bit adds ~4x throughput but costs ~2.7% LongBench, and the broader literature (KIVI, RotateKV, OSCAR) shows 2-bit KV is outlier-fragile — BitDecoding only survives it via the FP16 residual + channel-wise scaling, so 2-bit is "acceptable-with-loss," not preserved-quality.
assessment.delivery: CIPHER would HOST it, not invent it — but NOT through its existing cuBLAS/cutlass GEMM-interposition path. BitDecoding is an ATTENTION kernel (FlashDecoding-style), and CIPHER's own prior work (ra-realvllm) already flagged attention as FlashAttn, NOT cuBLAS, hence UNCOVERED by GEMM interception. So shipping this means swapping/hosting a different attention backend kernel under vLLM (like replacing FlashAttention with a low-bit-KV kernel), which is closer to a backend-kernel swap than to "hosting a quantized checkpoint." Feasible (code is open: OpenBitSys/BitDecoding, standalone CUDA kernels; KV quant is online so no model artifact to produce) but it lives OUTSIDE CIPHER's GEMM-substrate line and competes with already-upstream vLLM FP8/NVFP4 KV-cache support delivering ~1.5-2x at near-zero quality cost with zero custom kernel. The "no-pure-posthoc" codesign label is slightly misleading: the KV quantization itself IS purely post-hoc/online (no retrain); "codesign" here means the kernel must be co-designed with channel-wise scaling + a residual buffer, not that the model is retrained.
assessment.reasoning: The speedup is REAL on H100 (raises tokens/sec via tensor cores + reduced KV bandwidth, not paper FLOPs) and the quality cost is HONEST and post-hoc (4-bit -0.2%, no finetune) — so it clears the bar the founding post-hoc levers failed. I chose real-2x-hardware over overstated because the >=2x is genuinely achievable and measured, but flag two material caveats preventing a clean CIPHER win: (1) gain is CONDITIONAL on long context + batching — at CIPHER's short-context 7B-dense regime the realistic gain is well under 2x and often ~0; (2) it is an attention-path method, so it does NOT compose with CIPHER's GEMM-interposition substrate and overlaps heavily with already-shipping vLLM FP8/NVFP4 KV quant. Numbers cross-checked across arXiv v1/v2, the GitHub repo, and independent KV-quant literature; the "8.9x H100" figure is corroborated but is the batched-kernel-only number, not end-to-end (end-to-end ~3x, long-context only). 2-bit is not preserved-quality. Net: a real hardware lever, but a long-context attention lever sitting off CIPHER's current substrate line, not a drop-in 2x for general 7B-dense serving.

method.name: KVQuant: per-channel pre-RoPE non-uniform KV quantization
method.math: 3-bit (and lower) KV quantization with: per-channel Key quantization (matches Key outlier-along-channel distribution), pre-RoPE Key quantization, per-layer sensitivity-weighted non-uniform datatypes (nuq), and per-vector dense-and-sparse outlier isolation. Reduces KV HBM footprint to break the memory-bandwidth wall in long-context decode.
method.measured_speedup: ~4.8x reduction in KV activation memory at 3-bit; enables Llama-7B at 1M context on a single A100-80GB (10M on 8 GPUs). Memory/capacity-driven throughput; the paper's headline is footprint and context-length, not a single decode-kernel speedup factor (vs BitDecoding which provides tensor-core kernel speedups).
method.measured_quality: <0.1 perplexity degradation at 3-bit on Wikitext-2 and C4 (Llama / Llama-2 / Llama-3 / Mistral). Near-lossless at 3-bit.
method.posthoc_possible: YES, post-hoc. Needs a one-time offline calibration to fit the non-uniform datatypes and outlier sets; no gradient finetune, no weight change. NeurIPS 2024.
method.hardware: A100-80GB (single and 8-GPU); applies to GPU long-context serving.

assessment.method: KVQuant: per-channel + pre-RoPE Key quantization, per-layer sensitivity-weighted non-uniform datatypes (nuq), per-vector dense-and-sparse outlier isolation; calibration-only (16 Wikitext-2 samples, no finetune). Target = KV-cache HBM footprint / memory-bandwidth wall in long-context decode, NOT GEMM FLOPs.
assessment.honest_gain: Quality is real and cheap: <0.1 PPL degradation at 3-bit (LLaMA-7B Wikitext-2 5.68 base -> 5.75 at nuq3-1%; Mistral/Llama-2/3 similar), calibration-only, no finetune -- the rare post-hoc-ish lever that preserves quality. BUT the speed claim is footprint/capacity, not a tensor-core throughput multiplier. Measured kernel speedup is only 1.2-1.6x (Key) / 1.3-1.7x (Value) matvec, on an A6000 at 4-bit, vs fp16 -- and that is the GENEROUS number. The headline '4.8x' is KV memory compression at 3-bit (-> 1M ctx on 1xA100, 10M on 8 GPUs at 2-bit), i.e. CAPACITY enabling longer context / larger batch, not tokens/sec at fixed shape. Honest expected gain on H100/7B-dense/preserved-quality: in the LONG-CONTEXT memory-bound decode regime ONLY, roughly 1.2-1.7x decode throughput from reduced KV bytes moved (and larger feasible batch); ~1.0x (no gain, pure overhead) in short-context / compute-bound or prefill regimes. This is genuinely a bandwidth-relief lever (NOT FLOP-reduction-lowering-the-numerator): the founding research itself measured decode MFU 0.2-23% = memory-bound, and KV quant attacks exactly that wall -- fewer KV bytes per step = more tokens/sec without touching compute. The catch: KVQuant runs dequant on CUDA cores via lookup tables + a sparse CSR/CSC outlier matmul, which is FUNDAMENTALLY hard to map onto 2:4 / tensor cores. So it does NOT get the '2x peak from hardware-accelerated structure' that the prompt's gold standard requires. Successor BitDecoding (Mar 2025) exists precisely because of this: by inducing tensor-core-friendly layouts it beats QServe-class low-bit KV methods by up to 4.3x e2e and hits 8.9x kernel speedup on H100 -- evidence that KVQuant's CUDA-core LUT design leaves most of the throughput on the table.
assessment.delivery: HOST a co-designed checkpoint-equivalent (feasible, like hosting a quant) -- NOT invent. KVQuant needs no model retrain, only offline calibration (Fisher info + per-layer scales, a few minutes; <=6h for 65B). CIPHER could compute the nuq datatypes + per-channel pre-RoPE scales offline and host a 3-bit KV cache, dequantizing in its intercepted attention path -- structurally identical to how it hosts a quantized model. THE WALL is the kernel, not the math: per-channel pre-RoPE Keys + non-uniform LUT + per-vector dense-and-sparse outliers are incompatible with the contiguous fp16 per-token layout that PagedAttention/FlashAttention assume. Delivering real H100 throughput requires a CUSTOM FUSED attention+dequant kernel injected into vLLM's attention path -- which is exactly the in-graph / vLLM-source-cooperation wall CIPHER's own R.A work already hit (vLLM rejects external graph mutation; hosting needs source cooperation / eager). On a substrate-legal cuBLAS/cutlass-interposition surface, KVQuant's attention-side gains are mostly OUT OF REACH; CIPHER intercepts GEMM, but KVQuant's win lives in the attention/softmax/KV-load path (FlashAttn), which CIPHER's prior work flagged as the uncovered blind spot.
assessment.reasoning: Adversarial verification across the NeurIPS-2024 paper (arxiv 2401.18079 v5) and 3 successor/critique sources. (1) Is the speedup real on H100? PARTIALLY: real but small (1.2-1.7x) and measured on A6000 4-bit, CUDA-core-bound; no tensor-core acceleration, so it does NOT raise tokens/sec the way 2:4 sparse tensor cores (2x peak) would. The big number (4.8x) is footprint/capacity, not throughput -- exactly the FLOP-vs-MFU trap the prompt warns about, except here it is a memory-byte reduction that DOES help in the memory-bound decode regime, just modestly and only long-context. (2) Quality honest? YES -- <0.1 PPL at 3-bit is calibration-only and reproducible across Llama/Mistral; one of the few levers where quality survives without finetune. I tag verdict 'real-but-needs-finetune' not because KVQuant needs finetune (it does not), but because realizing its throughput potential on H100 needs co-designed SYSTEMS work (a tensor-core fused kernel a la BitDecoding) that is the moral equivalent of 'needs more than dropping in a frozen artifact' -- the closest schema option; 'flop-reduction-not-throughput' would be wrong since it is bandwidth not FLOPs, and 'overstated'/'quality-killer' are both inaccurate. (3) CIPHER ships: host (feasible) the calibrated cache; cannot get the speedup without a custom fused attention kernel = the known vLLM-cooperation wall. (4) Honest gain: 1.2-1.7x decode in long-context memory-bound regime, ~0 elsewhere, quality preserved. Net: a genuine but modest, kernel-gated, long-context-only lever; the math is sound and quality-cheap, but the deliverable throughput on H100 is bottlenecked by the same attention-path/in-graph integration wall CIPHER already measured, and is dominated by tensor-core successors. Sources: arxiv.org/html/2401.18079v5; arxiv.org/abs/2503.18773 (BitDecoding); themlsurgeon TurboQuant critique; KIVI 2402.02750.

research.summary:
SINGLE MOST PROMISING NEW LEVER FOR CIPHER (H100): EAGLE-3 speculative decoding. It is the only 2025-2026 lever that (a) delivers a measured 1.4-1.7x on H100 specifically, (b) is provably LOSSLESS (preserves the base model's exact output distribution under standard draft-and-verify, so "quality-preserving" is a guarantee, not an empirical hope), and (c) has tiny, CIPHER-compatible model-side cost: train a ~277MB draft head on ~54K examples in ~1.5 H100-hours, no base-model retrain. CIPHER can host the draft head exactly the way it hosts a quantized checkpoint, and vLLM already ships EAGLE-3 natively.

CRITICAL HONEST CAVEAT THAT REORDERS THE FRONTIER FOR A HOPPER SUBSTRATE: The most-hyped 2025-2026 lever, NVFP4/MXFP4 + quantization-aware distillation (QAD), gives its 2.2-3.6x throughput ONLY on Blackwell (B200/GB200) 5th-gen tensor cores. On H100 there is NO native FP4 tensor core; vLLM loads NVFP4 weights via a Marlin software fallback that reduces memory footprint but yields no throughput gain over FP8. So the headline 2x+ FP4 numbers are NOT available to CIPHER on H100 as a SPEED lever — they are a memory/capacity lever only. This directly answers the founding question: yes, co-design (QAD) restores quality at 4-bit (≤1% degradation, even +2% on AIME for DeepSeek-R1), but the hardware-accelerated 2x requires Blackwell silicon, not math.

FLOP-vs-MFU honesty (the explicit ask): The user's instinct is correct. (1) EAGLE-3 does NOT reduce FLOPs or raise MFU — it raises tokens/sec by trading idle memory-bound decode bandwidth for redundant compute (batches multiple candidate tokens per memory load). That is precisely why it works at batch=1-4 (memory-bound, MFU~0.2-23% per the founding's own decode numbers) and COLLAPSES to break-even at batch>=32 where decode becomes compute-bound. It exploits the same memory-bound regime the founding identified, but unlike W4A16 it is lossless and hardware-neutral. (2) 2:4 sparse tensor cores are the ONLY structure that raises peak compute (2x), but measured sparsity-alone gain is just 1.1-1.2x and the published numbers are A100/A5000-class, not H100; needs 13B-token distillation. (3) Activation sparsity (TEAL) and W4A16 reduce the numerator / are memory-bound-only (the founding already found W4A16 fires only at M=1). NONE of the post-hoc-failed founding levers are resurrected into a hardware-accelerated H100 speedup by co-design at 7B-dense; the realizable H100 win is the orthogonal, lossless speculative-decode lever.

methods.name: EAGLE-3 speculative decoding (TOP PICK for H100) — lightweight trained draft head + lossless draft-and-verify
methods.math: Not a matrix-factorization/quantization lever. A small draft network (reuses the target model's hidden features from low/mid/high layers) autoregressively proposes k draft tokens; the target model verifies all k in ONE forward pass via tree/chain attention. Standard speculative-sampling verification makes the output provably IDENTICAL to the unaccelerated target distribution (exact-match for greedy; rejection-sampling correction for sampling). Speedup = accepted_tokens_per_verify; it converts a memory-bandwidth-bound decode (1 token per weight load) into amortized multi-token-per-load. Reduces NO FLOPs and does NOT raise MFU — it monetizes idle bandwidth in the memory-bound decode regime, which is exactly why it decays as batch grows and the model becomes compute-bound.
methods.measured_speedup: On H100 (HF/vLLM eng blog, Llama-3.1-8B validation + GLM-4.7-Flash 3B-active): batch=1 1.39x (8.18->5.89 ms/token; 120->168 tok/s); batch=32 1.70x system throughput (259->440 tok/s), 1.30x per-request latency. vLLM EAGLE-3.1 (GB200, Kimi-K2): 2.03x at concurrency 1, 1.71x at C=4, 1.66x at C=16. Independent reports: 1.8-2.0x e2e across AngelSlim-trained models; 2.3x at batch=4. DECAY: ~break-even at batch>=32, negligible at batch>=64 (decode becomes compute-bound). Acceptance measured ~40% of k=6 proposals, ~2.4 accepted tokens/verify.
methods.measured_quality: LOSSLESS BY CONSTRUCTION — output is exactly the target model's distribution (greedy: bit-identical token stream; sampling: distribution-preserving via rejection sampling). Multiple primary sources state this is an algorithmic guarantee, not an empirical measurement. No perplexity/accuracy degradation is possible from the speculation step itself.
methods.posthoc_possible: PARTIAL: the base model is untouched and its outputs are unchanged (so it IS post-hoc with respect to the served model and ideal for a host like CIPHER). But it requires TRAINING a small draft head (not pure post-hoc). Cost measured: 277MB draft checkpoint, ~54K examples (ShareGPT/UltraChat/PerfectBlend), 1h26m on a single H100. CIPHER can host the draft head the same way it hosts a quantized checkpoint; vLLM has native EAGLE-3 support, so integration under unmodified vLLM is realistic.
methods.hardware: H100-native and hardware-neutral (no special tensor cores needed). This is its key advantage over FP4. Best in low-concurrency / memory-bound decode; mandate --speculative-disable-by-batch-size ~32 to avoid net loss at high concurrency.

methods.name: NVFP4 / MXFP4 4-bit + Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD) — MOST HYPED, but Blackwell-only for SPEED
methods.math: Microscaling FP4: weights+activations in E2M1 (4-bit) with per-block scales — NVFP4 block=16 with FP8 (e4m3) scales + a second-level tensor scale; MXFP4 block=32 with E8M0 scales (NVFP4 is more accurate due to finer blocks). Two-level microscaling preserves dynamic range. QAD = fine-tune/distill the FP4 model against the BF16 teacher to recover the quality PTQ loses. This is genuine co-design (the founding's W4A16 was post-hoc PTQ); QAD is the calibration+distill the founding lacked.
methods.measured_speedup: 2.2x end-to-end / up to 3.6x layer-wise vs FP16 — but ONLY on Blackwell B200 5th-gen FP4 tensor cores. ON H100: NO throughput gain. vLLM loads NVFP4 weights on H100/A100 via a Marlin FP4 software fallback that cuts memory footprint (3.5x vs FP16, 1.8x vs FP8) but does NOT beat FP8 throughput. Akamai measured +32% tokens vs FP8 on RTX Pro 6000 (Blackwell), not Hopper. So for CIPHER's H100 this is a memory/capacity lever, not a speed lever.
methods.measured_quality: With QAD/PTQ: <=1% accuracy degradation FP8->NVFP4 on DeepSeek-R1-0528 key LM tasks; +2% on AIME 2024 (noise/regularization). MR-GPTQ recovers 98-99% of FP16 accuracy at NVFP4. QAD report (NVIDIA Nemotron, models ~9B-30B incl. 12B-VL) claims near-BF16 parity and closes the residual PTQ gap on reasoning/instruction-following (exact per-benchmark deltas not cleanly extractable from the PDF — flagged as not fully verified).
methods.posthoc_possible: PARTIAL: PTQ alone (no training) often within ~1% at NVFP4; QAD (needs training, 'relatively small' token budget, not pure post-hoc) closes the last gap on hard reasoning tasks. CIPHER could host an NVFP4 checkpoint, but on H100 it buys memory, not speed.
methods.hardware: Blackwell-ONLY for the 2x+ throughput (B200/GB200/RTX Pro 6000, 5th-gen tensor cores). H100/Hopper has no native FP4 path — Marlin software fallback = memory savings only. This is the single most important caveat for a Hopper substrate.

methods.name: 2:4 semi-structured sparsity + knowledge distillation (Sparse Llama / SparseGPT+SquareHead) — the ONLY peak-FLOP-raising structure
methods.math: Prune weights to 2:4 pattern (2 of every 4 zero) so Sparse Tensor Cores skip zeros and DOUBLE peak matmul throughput. Co-design: SparseGPT one-shot prune, then SquareHead layerwise KD to recover quality (the calibration/distill the founding's post-hoc Wanda-style pruning lacked). This is the canonical 'hardware-accelerated structure' the user names: 2:4 raises peak compute, unlike FLOP-cutting which only lowers the numerator.
methods.measured_speedup: Sparsity-ALONE only 1.1-1.2x (the honest number — far below the theoretical 2x; real GEMMs don't hit peak and decode is memory-bound). Combined sparse+W4A16 quant: 3.0x single-stream on A5000/A6000, 2.1x on A100; throughput 1.2-1.8x. NOTE: published numbers are A100/Ampere-class — the Red Hat article gives NO H100 single-stream/throughput figure for the sparse model, so the H100-specific gain is UNVERIFIED here. A separate result cites 1.27x via SparseGPT+vLLM and 1.18x on H100 Qwen-14B (decode memory-bound).
methods.measured_quality: 98.4% recovery on Open LLM Leaderboard v1, 97.3% on Mosaic Eval Gauntlet; full recovery (sometimes exceeding dense) on GSM8K/code/chat after fine-tuning. So quality IS recoverable with co-design — but at real model-side cost.
methods.posthoc_possible: NO for quality at 7B-dense: one-shot 2:4 prune without recovery drops accuracy; recovery needs 13B-token KD pretraining (~26 H100-hours on 32 H100s) + task fine-tuning. CIPHER could host the resulting sparse checkpoint, but producing it is a pretrain-scale effort, and the sparsity-alone speed payoff on H100 is only ~1.1-1.2x.
methods.hardware: H100/Ampere Sparse Tensor Cores (2x peak for 2:4). The lever the user calls out as 'actually raises tok/s' — but measured realized gain is modest (1.1-1.2x from sparsity) and the big 2-3x numbers bundle in quantization and are Ampere-measured.

methods.name: TEAL training-free dynamic activation sparsity (vs CATS) — FLOP/memory-bound lever, no co-design, no peak-compute gain
methods.math: Magnitude-threshold zeroing of low-magnitude activation entries across ALL hidden states (not just SwiGLU gate), turning dense matmuls into sparse ones that skip rows/cols of weight loads. Training-free (just calibrate per-layer thresholds). Directly addresses the founding's 'SwiGLU too dense post-hoc' failure by sparsifying activations model-wide rather than relying on intrinsic ReLU-style sparsity.
methods.measured_speedup: Wall-clock DECODE speedup up to 1.53x at 40% sparsity and 1.8x at 50% sparsity (Llama-2/3, Mistral 7B-70B). Memory-bound regime only (reduces weight bytes loaded per token); does NOT use sparse tensor cores, so it lowers the numerator / is a bandwidth play — gains shrink at high batch like all memory-bound levers.
methods.measured_quality: Near-zero degradation at 25% sparsity; minimal at 40%; degrades past 50%. Outperforms CATS and ReLUfication on WikiText + 6-task LM-harness aggregate. Compatible with weight quantization for stacking.
methods.posthoc_possible: YES — training-free, calibration-only; CIPHER-friendly (no checkpoint change beyond threshold metadata). But it is a FLOP/bandwidth reduction, not hardware-accelerated structure, so it does NOT raise MFU and fades at high concurrency.
methods.hardware: H100-native, needs a custom sparse GEMM/GEMV kernel to realize the bandwidth saving (kernel availability is the practical gate). No special tensor cores.

methods.name: Speculative decoding x quantization CO-DESIGN (QSpec / Spec-meets-Quant) — stacking caveat
methods.math: Combine a low-precision draft with verification (QSpec uses complementary quant schemes: fast W4A4-style drafting verified by W4A16); or run EAGLE on top of a quantized base. Goal: stack the memory-bandwidth win of quantization with the multi-token-per-load win of speculation.
methods.measured_speedup: Stacking is SUBLINEAR / often disappointing: applying EAGLE-2 on W4A16/W4A8 yields LIMITED additional speedup because tree-verification compute overhead eats the 4-bit bandwidth benefit. QSpec recovers some of this: 1.38x over W4A16 across settings, peak 1.64x. Net: do not assume EAGLE's 1.4-1.7x multiplies cleanly onto a 4-bit base on H100.
methods.measured_quality: QSpec preserves quality (verification keeps target-model fidelity; the aggressive quant is confined to the draft). Aggressive joint W4A4 on the TARGET degrades multi-step reasoning — keep the verified target at >=W4A16/FP8.
methods.posthoc_possible: PARTIAL: base quantization can be PTQ (post-hoc) but the draft head needs training; the combination is what CIPHER would host. Important for CIPHER because it already ships a W4A16/Marlin path — adding EAGLE on top will NOT simply add its full speedup.
